  recorded when the call returns, and the scheduler commits. The executor is
  told of the labels a commit stored when the replica applies it, through the
  storage notification whose source is that transaction. *Alternative:* a
  transaction of the runtime for each of the executor's, as on the adapter of
  milestone 1, committed by the adapter and not by the scheduler. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/piece.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `RuntimeTransactions.within` and its callers in `piece.ts`.
- **P54. Which rows are documents of their own is read from the plan when the
  piece starts.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner
  ruling. It builds what the owner decided with Z86, and the choice here is
  where the rule lives. *The case:* the boundary is static per collection
  (question 356), and the crate does not emit it. *Decision:*
  `rowDocumentCollections` of `base/pattern-compiler/exec/row-documents.ts`
  names a collection whose construct is `map`, written in no element body,
  with an output below a row, and whose source is a slot whose schema declares
  the array or its members as cells, an output whose body gives a reference at
  each member (`Body.outputs` at `*`), or a `filter` over such a source. That
  is a `map` over an array of references that the type declares as references,
  or over the result of a construct that yields references. A `map` over an
  array of plain values in place keeps its rows in place whatever the data
  holds, also when it is given an array of references at run time. The
  document of a row is the entity named by the hash of the array's document,
  its path and the key of the row, and the array holds the runtime's link to
  it with no schema. `CompiledPieceOptions.rows` set to `in-place` stores
  every row in its array. *Alternative:* the crate emits the boundary as a
  member of the collection, which is where the documents put it ("decided per
  construct by the compiler from the two templates",
  `compiled-pattern-language-integration.md`, "Labels of large derived
  collections"). *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts`
  and `layout-labels.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* `exec/row-documents.ts`
  and the plan format.
- **P55. The derivation action of a compiled piece opts out of the scheduler's
  delay for slow actions.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* the scheduler delays by 100 ms an action whose
  runs took 50 ms or more on average over at least three runs
  (`AUTO_DEBOUNCE_THRESHOLD_MS` of the scheduler's `gates.ts`). The derivation
  of a piece is one action for all its cones (P51), so after three slow
  derivations every event of the piece waited 100 ms: an edit of one member of
  a `map` over an array declared as references took 105 ms at 1,000 rows, of
  which 5 ms were work. *Decision:* the action opts out
  (`Scheduler.setNoDebounce`). *Alternative:* a scheduler action for each cone
  instance (the alternative of P51). *Tests:* none; measured with
  `compare/runner-path.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* one call in `piece.ts`.
- **P56. The read of a slot that observes which children a container has gives
  the members as references and reads none of them.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* `Host.slot` of
  `exec/executor.ts` read the array of an `enumeration` slot under the schema
  of the slot's place, which followed each link and registered the root of
  each member's document as read. For an array of references,
  `topics.get().length` and every `lift` handed the array then ran again for a
  change of any field of any member. *Decision:* the read gives the members as
  references and reads none, where no slot of the cone reads a child, or below
  one, as a value or a shape, or where every body of the cone that is handed
  the container declares a handle at each child (`Host.#handsHandles`). A cone
  with a body that is handed the members with the container reads them. It
  applies to an array of references; the members of an array of plain values
  in place are in the array's document. *Alternative:* the read under the type
  of the place, which is linear in the members for every change of one.
  *Tests:* `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/handle-reads.test.ts` and
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* `Host.slot`.
- **P57. The plan holds the schema of the type a body declares for a handle,
  and a read under a schema that declares its members registers the positions
  of those members.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner
  ruling. It answers question 359. *The case:* the plan said `handle: true`
  for a `handle` entry of `Body.reads` and held no schema, so `handle.get()`
  read under the schema of the place the handle is to and registered the root
  of the member's document. *Decision:* the crate emits the schema of the
  declared type as `ReadInput.schema` and, for an `identity` entry of
  `Body.computed`, as `ComputedInput.schema` (`body_record` of `src/plan.rs`);
  the type of a destructured parameter is taken from its annotation. The
  executor reads through the handle under that schema (`Handle.#typed`), and
  the read registers the positions of the members the schema declares and not
  the position of the record, where the record holds a member the schema does
  not declare (`Store.locate`). A record all of whose members are declared is
  registered at its own position, which marks the same readers with one
  registration. *Alternative:* registering every declared member of the schema
  of the place, which was tried and withdrawn: it marks the same readers as
  the root and gives longer write records. *Tests:*
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/handle-fields.test.ts`,
  `handle-reads.test.ts` and `base/pattern-compiler/tests/plan.rs`. *If
  decided otherwise:* the two schema members of the plan, `Store.locate` and
  `Handle.#typed`.
- **P58. The label of a write record is formed again when a label its inputs
  read changed and the record is not given again, whether or not a value
  changed with the label.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. It answers question 357. *The case:* under the rule of
  milestone 4 a change that the store did not report as one of labels alone
  formed no label again, on the ground that the change of the value runs the
  cones that read it. A record can read the label through another position: a
  writer that changes the note of a topic under a schema with one more clause
  changes the label that a read of the title consumes, and no cone that read
  the title runs. The rows and the output derived from them kept their labels,
  an under-label. *Decision:* `Instance.labelsChanged` forms the label again
  for every record that read a changed label and is not given again. The
  adapter tells the piece of a commit of another writer that changed a label
  the executor read, which runs the derivation. So that the rule does not form
  labels again for every write, the adapter compares label entries by their
  canonical text and says for each change whether a read of a class at a
  position consumes the label it consumed before (`LabelChange.unchanged`),
  and the executor forms no label again for a record none of whose positions
  consumes another label (`#readsChangedLabel`): a `Cell.set` of one field of
  a labeled document stores an entry at the field's path under the label of
  the root and writes the root's entry with its members in another order,
  which without the comparison formed the labels of 1,014 records again for
  one edit at 1,000 topics. *Alternative:* the rule of milestone 4, with the
  store deciding for each reader whether a value it read changed, which the
  store does not know. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts` and
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/transaction-hooks.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* `Instance.labelsChanged` and `LabelChange.unchanged`.
- **P59. The row documents a `lift` writes are one reader of the labels the
  `lift` read, and a row whose value and whose label inputs stayed is given no
  record.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling.
  It extends P48 and answers the second half of question 358. *The case:* the
  records of P48 were given for every row on each run of the `lift`, 1,010 for
  an edit at 1,000 topics, and a change of a label alone did not form them
  again. *Decision:* the records of the documents a `lift` writes for its rows
  are registered as one reader of the labels of what the body read, under a
  key of the cone instance (`#recordCreated` and `#noteRecord` of
  `exec/executor.ts`), and a change of a label there forms the label of every
  row again (`#relabelCreated`). When the body runs again, a row that holds
  what it held is given no record where the labels the body read are those it
  had read: the identifiers of the labels at the positions read, in the
  classes `value`, `identity` and `shape`, are kept as a set (`#labelsRead`),
  and where no position left and no label changed the positions that entered
  are asked alone. A position that the transaction in progress wrote has no
  identifier, and every row is then given its record. P64 keeps a create by a
  handler out of that case. *Alternative:* one record per row with the reads the
  body had
  made when it wrote the row, which is one entry of the table of inputs per
  row. *Tests:* `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/transaction-hooks.test.ts`
  and `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* those four functions.
- **P60. A member added at the end of an array of row documents is written as
  the number of members and the link added.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* the executor gives the record
  of a change of the members of a kept `map` as one that names the array
  (`membersChanged`), and the runtime refuses a record that names a path the
  transaction did not write, so the array of links was written whole for every
  change of its members, `N` links. This is a `map` over an array declared as
  references whose rows are documents. *Decision:* for an addition at the end
  the transaction writes the number of members and each link added and no
  write of the array itself. The record of the array is recorded as that of a
  write that left its path as it was, and again for each path written, so that
  the number and each added link have the label of the membership and not the
  join of everything the transaction read (`#recordAppended` of
  `transactions.ts`). An entry at the position of an added link stays until
  the array is next written at or above it. A prepend and a removal write the
  array of links whole, with the record of the array and of the row that
  entered. *Alternative:* the records of a change of members in place
  (`PlanWrite.enumeration` with `moves`), which the runtime has for a
  handler's splice of a stored list; its label is stored as the `enumerate`
  entry and labels no member, where the record of a kept `map` labels the
  array. *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts`. *If
  decided otherwise:* `#recordAppended` (question 365).
- **P61. A write by another writer into the document of a row is applied, and
  one of the array of links is reported and not applied.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a derived array
  is the executor's to write, and another writer can write it through the
  runtime. The executor holds each row of a derived array by its key, and
  after a write of the array by another its account of which keys are stored
  would be wrong. *Decision:* a write into the document of a row is
  applied to the row the executor holds, at the row's position. A write of the
  array of links, or above it, is reported to the piece
  (`CompiledPiece.refusals`) and not applied. With rows in place the same
  write is not applied and nothing reports it. *Alternative:* the piece writes
  the array again from what it holds at its next derivation, with the record
  of the array, which is the plan (question 366). *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* the change channel of `piece.ts`.
- **P62. After a refused commit the executor's documents are those the storage
  holds for what the transaction wrote.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* the executor has gone on when
  the scheduler commits. Where the preparation of Contextual Flow Control or
  the store refuses the commit, the executor's documents are ahead of the
  storage, and a derivation could store, under the labels of what the storage
  holds, a value computed from what the refused transaction wrote. A hook that
  asked the preparation before the executor ended an event's transaction was
  built and removed: the scheduler reads through the transaction after the
  handler returns, and the runtime refuses a transaction that was read after
  it was prepared. *Decision:* when the refusal is known, the adapter reads
  from the replica what the storage holds for each document of the executor
  that the transaction wrote, and the piece takes it in place of what the
  executor holds (`Instance.restore`), which marks what read those documents,
  and runs the derivation. A document the storage does not hold is removed,
  and with the result document of an instance that a function body made, the
  instance, so a handler that runs again makes both again. The result document
  of an instance is taken with the rows of each of its collections left out,
  and nothing of it counts as stored: the next derivation stores each path
  that differs and every row. The preparation refuses within the call of
  `commit`, so the documents are restored before the scheduler runs the
  derivation. The store answers later; the derivation that ran in between read
  what the handler wrote and is refused with it, and both are restored.
  *Alternative:* the withdrawal of one derived write of milestone 6, with
  verified units in the prepared digest, which is not built. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/refused-commit.test.ts` with the fixture
  `refused-commit.tsx`: a handler's write of a text that holds a secret into a
  cell that admits no such clause, under `enforce-strict`; the next event
  after it; a handler whose commit meets a write of another session; and the
  same with a derivation that had added a row. Not covered: a handler that the
  scheduler runs again after a conflict, and a refused commit of a transaction
  that created an instance (question 367). *If decided otherwise:*
  `Instance.restore` and its caller in `piece.ts`.
- **P63. The load of a compiled piece in three kinds of transactions, as a plan:
  replaced by P65, which builds it.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22;
  it is no owner ruling. *As first decided,* with nothing built. *The case:* the
  creation and the first derivation are one commit. At 2,000 topics it is past
  the memory server's limit of 1,000,000 array slots and record members in one
  client message, and its preparation is the number of targets times the number
  of reads. *The plan:* first, the documents the instance makes for itself, its
  argument and its state, in a transaction of their own, committed first, so
  that a binding of a later transaction that passes through the argument
  observes a stored label. Second, each row that is a document of its own, with
  the records of the change that makes it, in a transaction that holds at most
  `K` rows; a row goes there only where each record of it has inputs with no
  position the first derivation itself staged and none is a record without
  inputs, whose label is the join of the transaction, since a transaction of
  rows has read nothing. Third, the result document with the links to the rows,
  and everything else, in the transaction the caller commits, which holds every
  read of the derivation. *Replaced* by P65 (prototype note 603), which builds
  the three kinds and differs from the plan in three points. The transaction of
  the creation makes the reads the caller had made in the handed transaction,
  where the plan has it read nothing, which under-labels the argument. A row
  goes into a transaction of rows only where one of its records is of the row
  whole and no transaction of the load has written its document. And a load into
  a transaction the caller wrote into is not split. *If decided otherwise:* see
  P65.
- **P64. The first derivation of an instance a handler made is a transaction of
  its own, committed before the derivation of what reads the instance.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22, which the ruling Z87 of the same day
  admits: the derivations a batch made stale are each evaluated once, and two
  commits behind one event are within the ruling. *The case:* a handler that
  makes an instance
  stores its two documents in the event's transaction. With one derivation
  transaction behind the event, the first derivation of the instance is in the
  transaction that also runs every `lift` over the list that holds the new
  member. The labels of what those `lift`s read of the new member are then
  staged and have no identifier, so each row a `lift` writes is given its record
  again (P59): on Topics every row of `crossrefTable` and `namesTable`, 2,122
  write records for a create at 1,000 topics in the measurement of the second
  round. *Decision:* `Instance.settleMade` of
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/executor.ts` derives the instances a handler made,
  and nothing else, in one derivation transaction. The derivation action of the
  piece runs it first, invalidates itself, and runs again for the rest, and the
  scheduler commits the two apart. A reader between the two finds the new member
  with its result and the board's derived outputs without it, which is what the
  handler's own commit already shows with less. *Cost:* the new member reads the
  outputs of the board it is handed (`mentionable`, the pivot and its index)
  once in its own transaction and again when they change, about 5 positions a
  topic more for each create. *Measured:* a create on `filing-order` at 1,000
  topics gives 91 write records and takes 1,034 ms. *Alternative:* the adapter
  names a label that the transaction in progress stages, which keeps one
  transaction and needs the runtime's table of labels to hold labels that are
  not stored. *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/created-members.test.ts`
  with the fixture `created-members.tsx`: the row of a member a handler made;
  the member derived in a transaction before the one that derives what reads it;
  and no more write records, and no more labels named, for one more member where
  the list is longer. *If decided otherwise:* `Instance.settleMade` and its call
  in the derivation action of `runtime/runner/src/compiled/piece.ts`.
- **P65. The load of a compiled piece commits the creation, and then the row
  documents in bounded transactions, before the transaction it was handed; a
  load into a transaction the caller wrote into stays whole.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It replaces the plan P63. *The
  case:* a load in one commit holds 8,011 documents at 2,000 topics, past the
  memory server's limit of 1,000,000 array slots and record members in one
  client message. *Decision:* `RuntimeTransactions.within` of
  `runtime/runner/src/compiled/transactions.ts` takes `loadRows`, and
  `startCompiledPiece` passes `CompiledPieceOptions.loadRows`, 250 unless given.
  First, the creation, the documents the instance makes for itself, is a
  transaction of the adapter, committed when the executor ends it, and what it
  wrote then counts as stored. It makes the reads the handed transaction had
  made when the load began: the documents of the creation hold the argument,
  which the caller can have computed from what it read, and a transaction that
  read nothing would store them with no label, an under-label. Second, for each
  change of the result during the load, the adapter takes the row documents
  whose write records name stored positions alone (`#namesStoredAlone`: no
  position the load wrote, no `output` and no `staged` binding), that include a
  record for the row whole, and that no transaction of the load has written. It
  writes each into a transaction of rows with its records and a table of inputs
  of that transaction, and commits that transaction at `loadRows` rows and at
  the end of the change, so that none is open when the executor next reads or
  writes. Third, the rest, the links to the rows among it, is written into the
  handed transaction. Fourth, a load whose handed transaction holds a write of
  the caller is written into that transaction whole: the positions the caller
  staged are readable in that transaction alone, and a row stored by another
  transaction would read them as absent, an under-label. Where the preparation
  refuses a transaction of the load, the handed transaction is aborted. *What a
  reader may observe between the transactions:* after the creation, the
  argument, the empty result and the state documents; after a transaction of
  rows, row documents that no document links to. *Why it is sound for labels:*
  each row is stored with the records it has in a load in one transaction, and
  those records name stored positions alone, so the label they instantiate to is
  the label the row has when the load is done; no path of a row is without a
  record, since one is of the row whole; and a read through a link that the
  handed transaction writes joins the label of the link's position. *What it
  changes in the stored labels:* at `topics`, `names`, `namesTable` and `index`
  of the Topics boards a read consumes less than after a load in one
  transaction, which over-labels them (question 375). *Open:* a handed
  transaction that is not committed or is refused leaves the creation and the
  rows stored; the documents a `lift` writes for its rows stay in the handed
  transaction (question 374); and whether a start may be several commits at all
  is the owner's (question 368). *Alternative:* one commit with the memory
  server's limit raised, which `loadRows` set to `Infinity` gives. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/row-documents.test.ts`, "the load in bounded
  transactions": the rows are committed in transactions of at most the given
  number before the result; each row holds the label entries a load in one
  transaction stores; the documents of the creation are stored under what the
  caller read before the start; a load into a transaction the caller wrote into
  is in that transaction; and a change of a member after such a load is taken.
  *If decided otherwise:* the `loadRows` option, `#rowsToStoreApart` and
  `#commitRows` of `transactions.ts`.
- **P66. A record of a transaction's reads keeps the metadata object it was
  recorded with once a boundary pass has asked for the reads, and a site that
  reads under a metadata object of its own freezes it.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It is the remedy that questions
  347 and 351 name, and whether it goes to `main` is the owner's (question 347).
  *The case:* `InputReadView.reads` of `runtime/runner/src/cfc/prepare.ts` is
  asked once for each target a boundary pass verifies. Without the change each
  ask compares every read record of the transaction with the copy the view holds
  and classifies every distinct metadata object again; the write path records
  its reads of each destination under a metadata object it builds for that read,
  so a transaction that wrote 1,000 cells holds 6,003 distinct metadata objects
  for 7,003 records. The work is the number of targets times the number of
  reads, on today's path with no experimental option. *Decision:* the
  transaction freezes the records it lists when the view asks, and returns a
  count that advances when the list gains a record or is emptied
  (`freezeReadActivityRecords` of `runtime/runner/src/storage/interface.ts`,
  implemented in `v2-transaction.ts` and passed on by the two wrappers of
  `extended-storage-transaction.ts`). With the same list and the same count the
  view compares no record. It classifies again only the distinct metadata
  objects that are not frozen, and the sites of the runner that build a metadata
  object for a read freeze it. A transaction that does not offer the call, or
  hands out another list, is compared record by record. *What differs for a
  caller:* a record the view has copied refuses another metadata object with a
  `TypeError`, where without the change the view finds the replacement at its
  next ask. A metadata object that is changed in place is found either way. No
  code of the runtime replaces the metadata of a record. *The classification,*
  which is the build agent's and is not reviewed: a host arrangement in the
  terms of `docs/development/cfc-spec-correspondence.md`, since the change
  decides nothing and stores nothing, with that one difference in what a caller
  of the transaction may do during a pass, which fails loudly and closed.
  *Measured:* writing 10,000 cells in one transaction with no piece started has
  9.8 s of preparation without the change and 2.9 s with it; 1,000 cells, 0.17 s
  and 0.16 s. *Alternative:* the comparison of every record at each ask.
  *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/cfc/InputReadView.test.ts` counts the work with
  `InputReadView.recordsCompared` and `InputReadView.metadataObjectsClassified`:
  25 asks over 40 reads compare no record, and a transaction that wrote 40 cells
  has the view classify as many metadata objects as one that wrote 4. One test
  of that file replaced the metadata of a record and changes the object in
  place. The test directory of the runner passes, 2,157 files. *Where it is:*
  commit `42676da433` of the branch of milestone 3. *If decided otherwise:*
  `freezeReadActivityRecords`, the frozen metadata objects and the two counters.
- **P67. The grouping is the collection index the language has, `groupBy` and
  `keyBy` with `lookup`, and no new function.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It answers part (c) of question 370. *The
  case:* `crossrefIndexOf` of Topics groups the rows of a table by name, and a
  `lift` does it by reading every row. `language-subset.md` §4.4,
  `plan-and-label-templates.md` §3.17 and today's runtime
  (`IDerivable.groupBy` of `base/api/index.ts`) already have a grouping and a
  lookup by key; the crate's plan emitter refused both and the executor had
  neither. *Decision:* `xs.groupBy((x) => key)` and `xs.keyBy((x) => key)` in
  the reactive tier, with the callback grammar of a `map` callback, and
  `index.lookup(k)`. A key is a string, a number, a boolean or a cell; `null`
  and `undefined` leave the element out. Over an array of references a bucket
  holds the references of its members in source order; over an array of plain
  values in place, a reference by key to each member's position; over the
  result of another per-element construct, a reference to the row where the
  rows are documents (P77) and a copy of the row otherwise. The label rule is
  that of §3.17: the membership of a bucket is the source's membership joined
  with a `fold` of the key function's template over every element.
  *Alternative:* `Object.groupBy(xs, f)` inside a promoted `computed`, whose
  result is a plain record with no `lookup` and no place for a dependency on
  one key. *Tests:* `base/pattern-compiler/tests/plan.rs`,
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/collection-index.test.ts`, and
  `collection-index.test.ts`, `kept-index.test.ts` and `index-modes.test.ts`
  under `runtime/runner/test/compiled/`. *Not built:* `keys()` and
  `keyEntries()`. *If decided otherwise:* the arm of `Emitter::method` of
  `src/plan.rs` and `Index` of `exec/executor.ts`.
- **P68. The keyed join is a `map` whose body calls `lookup`, and a source that
  names several keys is spread with `flatMap` first.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It answers part (b) of question
  370. *The case:* `crossrefTable` of Topics gives for each topic the topics
  that mention it. *Decision:* no construct of its own. The rows are those of a
  `map` whose body calls `index.lookup(key)`: over an array of references each
  row is a document of its own where it is a record (P54), and over plain values
  in place or over the result of another per-element construct the rows are in
  place. A source that names several keys is first spread into one element for
  each (source, key) pair, as `topics.flatMap((from) => from.mentions.map((to)
  => ({ from, to }))).groupBy((pair) => pair.to)`. A row has the label of what
  its body reads of its own element and, for the lookup, the template of the key
  joined with the fold over every source, so a row whose key no source names
  depends on every source's key. *Alternative:* `joinBy(sources, (source) =>
  keys, (key, matches) => row)`, new surface that today's transformer refuses,
  with the label rule that a source that names no key of a row adds nothing to
  the row, which is an under-label; and a key function that returns an array of
  keys, which today's `groupBy` does not take. *Tests:* the fixture
  `keyed-join.tsx` with `exec/test/collection-index.test.ts` and
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/collection-index.test.ts`; the fixture
  `crossref.tsx` with the two `crossref.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* a
  record of the plan and a construct of the executor for the join.
- **P69. The membership of all buckets of an index is one label entry of the
  index's state document. Designed, not built.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* the fold over every member's
  key is one label for all buckets. Stored at each bucket it is `N` entries each
  as long as the fold, which is how `plan-and-label-templates.md` §3.17 and
  `execution-and-storage.md` §6.3 read. *Decision:* the index is one state
  document whose `buckets` member holds a record from the encoded key to the
  bucket, and the fold is stored once, as the entry of `buckets`; a read of a
  bucket, of a position in it, of its length, or of a key that is absent
  resolves to that entry, as a read of a row in place joins the `*` templates.
  Where a bucket holds copies of rows, the entry is also joined with a fold of
  the row's template over the source, an over-label of each bucket by the rows
  of the others. *As built:* the result document holds a label entry at the
  index, at each bucket and at `keys`, each with the fold, and the index is
  formed again whole as a record when a bucket changes. *What it leaves where
  each member has a clause of its own:* the one entry holds `N` clauses and
  every reader of any bucket consumes all of them; a row whose body reads its
  bucket stores `N` clauses, so `N` rows store `N` squared (questions 352 and
  379). *Alternative:* a document for each bucket with the one label in each
  (question 379). *Tests:* none, since it is not built. *If decided otherwise:*
  nothing built changes.
- **P70. The per-entry construct over a record is
  `Object.entries(record).map(f)` over a record that is an input, keyed by the
  entry's name.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner
  ruling. It answers part (a) of question 370. *The case:* `namesTable` of
  Topics is a row for each entry of a record of references. *Decision:* the
  crate takes `Object.entries(x).map(([name, value]) => row)`, where `x` is a
  name or a member read that is a path of an input, as a `Collection` of
  construct `map` over the slot of the record with `source.entries`, the record
  observed as `enumeration`; an element slot has the path `0` for the name and
  a path from `1` for the value. Over a record of references `value` is the
  reference at the entry; over a record of plain values in place it is the
  value there; `Object.entries` of a record the instance computed stays a plain
  array generated from scratch. The membership, the count, the order and the
  name of an entry have the label of the enumeration; a row has the label of
  what its body reads. *Alternative:* a method `record.mapEntries(f)` of a cell,
  which needs a method in `base/api/index.ts` and a lowering in today's
  transformer. *Not covered:* `Object.keys(x).map`, `Object.values(x).map`, and
  a `filter` or a `flatMap` over the entries, which stay expressions over the
  whole record; an entry removed and added again under one name within a
  transaction, where the row keeps its state. *Tests:* `tests/plan.rs`,
  `exec/test/record-entries.test.ts` and
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/record-entries.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* `Emitter::entries_of_record` and `Instance.#entries`.
- **P71. The sort by a key as a recognized comparator of `toSorted`: replaced by
  P85, which builds the method `sortBy`.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *As first decided,* with nothing built.
  *The case:* the `lift` `topicsByActivity` reads the sort key of every topic on
  an edit of one. *The plan:* `xs.toSorted((a, b) => key(a) - key(b))`, with the
  operands exchanged for a descending order and `key(a).localeCompare(key(b))`
  for texts, taken out of the function tier where the comparator has one of
  these forms; a `Collection` of construct `sort`. The method `sortBy` was the
  alternative, left to the owner because it needs a method in
  `base/api/index.ts`. *Replaced* by P85: the method is one arm of the emitter
  beside `groupBy`, where the comparator needs a recognizer of its two forms,
  and `localeCompare` follows the locale of the process. *If decided
  otherwise:* see P85.
- **P72. The collection of an index is recorded in the plan as a `Collection`
  whose `construct` is `groupBy` or `keyBy`, with no `Operation` record.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  `plan-and-label-templates.md` §3.17 has the index as an `Operation` of kind
  `index` and a `Collection` of construct `operation` over the receiver.
  *Decision:* one `Collection` whose body cone is the key function and whose
  `membership` is the template of a `filter`; `lookup` on a place that is such
  an output is a value derived from the key and the index's output, and `lookup`
  on a slot, an index the instance is handed, is a `pick` below the `buckets`
  member of the slot (§3.18). *Alternative:* the two records of §3.17.
  *Tests:* `tests/plan.rs`, the test of the fold of the key function and of the
  key that a `lookup` joins. *If decided otherwise:* `Emitter::collection` and
  `index_of_place` of `src/plan.rs`, and the executor's reading of the
  collection.
- **P73. A bucket lists its members in the order of the source.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  today's runtime gave the members of a bucket in another order than the
  source's for an array of cells in one probe. *Decision:* the source order, as
  `plan-and-label-templates.md` §3.17 states, kept under a move in the source
  and a member that returns to a bucket. *Alternative:* the order in which the
  members entered the bucket. *Tests:* `exec/test/collection-index.test.ts`.
  *If decided otherwise:* the insertion by position in `Index`. The probe of
  today's runtime was not examined.
- **P74. A slot that reads the value a reference in an upstream row names has
  the label of the upstream output joined with the label of that read.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It closes an
  under-label. *The case:* a `map` over an array of references whose row holds a
  member of its element holds a reference to where the element stores it, and
  the plan gives that output the `identity` slot of the position. A per-element
  construct over the result of that `map` whose body reads the value has a
  `value` slot of root `element`, which `Instance.bindSlot` bound to the
  upstream output alone, so the stored label held nothing of the label of the
  value at the position the reference names. *Decision:* `bindSlot` keeps,
  beside the upstream element, the stored positions that the read of the slot
  went through, where the slot does not observe `identity`. `SlotBinding` of the
  write record takes `through` beside `output` (`exec/plan-write.ts`,
  `runtime/runner/src/cfc/types.ts`), and `inputsFor` of
  `runtime/runner/src/cfc/plan-labels.ts` joins the label of that read with the
  label of the output: the confidentiality of both, and the integrity both
  carry. The site carries the `SPEC-PENDING` marker, since such a binding is in
  no clause of the specification. *Alternative:* a plan that gives the upstream
  output the `value` slot, which labels a row with what it does not hold.
  *Tests:* `chained-maps.test.ts` and `index-of-rows.test.ts` under
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/`, each with the rows as documents and in place.
  *If decided otherwise:* `SlotBinding.through` and its join (questions 392 and
  397).
- **P75. The key of an index and of a `lookup` is observed by its type, and a
  key of an unresolved type and a `lookup` by a cell in a handed index are
  refused.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling.
  *The case:* the key of `crossrefTable` is a cell. *Decision:*
  `Emitter::key_class` of `src/plan.rs` observes a key as `value` where its
  type is a scalar and as `identity` where it is a cell, an object or an
  unknown. A key whose type the crate does not resolve is listed as unsupported;
  the crate does not resolve the type of a row of a `map` written in the body of
  a `flatMap`, so the key function of an index over such rows has its parameter
  annotated. A `lookup` in an index of the same instance passes a cell key as
  the reference it is, and the executor files a cell under the address it names.
  A `lookup` by a cell in an index the instance is handed is listed as
  unsupported: the buckets of a stored index are members of a record that a
  `pick` chooses by a value. *Alternative:* a key read as a value always, which
  reads the content of a cell to compare it. *Tests:* `tests/plan.rs`, the test
  of the cell key and the two tests of the refusals. *If decided otherwise:*
  `key_class` and `Facts::cell_key` of `src/emit.rs`.
- **P76. The members of a bucket that a `lookup` gave are elements with the keys
  of the index's source.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* a `map` over a bucket was a `map` over an array of
  plain values that a computation returned, which keys each value by the salted
  hash of the value with every link followed. For pairs that hold references to
  topics that mention each other the hash walks a graph as a tree, and the
  fixture did not load at 50 topics. *Decision:* `Host.lookup` names the members
  as the elements of the index's source (`bucketElements`), with the keys they
  have there, and `Instance.#table` takes them. `Index` marks the buckets whose
  members differ when its assembly is formed again whole. *What stays:* the same
  hash for any other `map` over an array of plain values in place that hold
  references to documents that refer to each other (question 380).
  *Alternative:* the key of note 643 for every plain value, which is the plan
  of question 380. *Tests:* `exec/test/crossref.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* `bucketElements`.
- **P77. A kept index over rows that are documents holds references by key to
  the rows.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling.
  *The case:* a kept index over the result of another per-element construct held
  a copy of each row, so it was written when a row changed, and a read of a
  bucket keyed the copies by the hash of P76. *Decision:* where the rows are
  documents of their own (the `Instance` option `rowDocuments`, which
  `startCompiledPiece` sets from `rowDocumentCollections`),
  `Instance.indexRecord` gives a reference by key to the row at its place in the
  result; `Store.locate` finds a row of an array named in `Store.rowKeys` by its
  element key, and `RuntimeTransactions.#encode` writes the reference as a link
  to the row's document. The index is written when a member enters or leaves a
  bucket, and a read of a member reads the row's document under the row's label.
  Where the rows are in place the bucket holds copies. *Alternative:* copies in
  both layouts. *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/crossref.test.ts`. *If
  decided otherwise:* `Instance.indexRecord` and `Store.rowKeys`.
- **P78. The rows of a `map` over the entries of a record of references are
  documents.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling.
  It extends P54. *The case:* the rows of `Object.entries(names).map(([name,
  member]) => ({ member, name }))`. *Decision:* `rowDocumentCollections` of
  `exec/row-documents.ts` takes a `map` over the entries of a record whose
  schema declares its values as cells. A record declared with values of an
  unknown type keeps its rows in place, which is the case of `namesTable` on the
  two Topics boards. *Alternative:* rows in place for every record. *Tests:*
  the fixture `names-table.tsx` with
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/names-table.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  that arm of `rowDocumentCollections`.
- **P79. A read that finds what a reference names is no read of what is stored
  below the named position.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* the element table of a collection over an array of
  references, and the keys of the array, are formed from what each link names.
  Registered as reads of the named position and everything below it, they had a
  write to any field of any member mark every assembly over the array and
  report a read of every member to the transaction: 1,013 positions read for an
  edit of a title at 1,000 topics. *Decision:* `Position.own` of `exec/store.ts`
  marks such a read; `Store.changedSince` and the marking of readers in
  `Instance` take a write at the position for a change and a write below it for
  none. A document that comes to exist, or whose root is replaced by a link, is
  a write at the position. *Alternative:* the read of the whole document.
  *Tests:* `exec/test/crossref.test.ts`, the last three cases. *If decided
  otherwise:* `Position.own`. It changes what marks a reader and no record
  (question 395).
- **P80. A grouping of the result of another per-element construct is in the
  compiled language alone, and the two measured Topics boards do not run on
  today's runtime.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner
  ruling. *The case:* `groupBy` is declared on a cell of an array, the result of
  a `flatMap` or a `map` in a pattern body is typed as a plain array, and a cast
  to a cell type is refused by today's transformer and by the crate. The pivot
  of Topics and its index both group such a result. *Decision:* the boards
  `board-filing-order.tsx` and `board-sorted-references.tsx` use the grouping,
  and the arms `today` and `today-labeled` of the harness run `main.tsx`. The
  facts that the arm `runner` reads of each board at 100 topics equal those the
  arm `today-labeled` read of the same board with the three `lift`s.
  *Alternative that today's types take:* a key function that returns the list of
  mentions, so that the grouping is over the array of topic references itself;
  today's `groupBy` takes one key. *Tests:* the comparison of the facts at 100
  topics, which is a run of the harness and no test. *If decided otherwise:*
  `groupBy` declared for the result of a per-element construct in
  `base/api/index.ts`, with a lowering in today's transformer (question 382).
- **P81. A verb that passes a collection on to an instance it makes is a handler
  with cells in its state.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* `addTopic` as an `action` in the pattern body closes
  over the mention universe, the pivot and its index, and the executor hands a
  handler each value it closes over read whole (`Instance.#attempt`): every row
  and, through the references in the rows, every topic. *Decision:* on the two
  boards `addTopic` is a handler whose state declares the three as cells.
  *Alternative, the plan:* the crate observes a captured value that the body
  only passes on as `identity` (question 381). *Tests:* none of its own; the
  boards are measured. *If decided otherwise:* the boards.
- **P82. A change of a label that leaves an element of a folded collection in
  its group gives no record of the fold again.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a write by another writer
  changed the label entry at one field of a topic's document.
  `Instance.#regroupReaders` of `exec/executor.ts` updated the group of the
  element of the pivot that read the document and gave the record of every
  output whose template folds over the pivot again, whether or not the
  element's group changed. The index of the pivot by name is such an output, so
  an edit of any field of any topic gave a record of the result document, and
  the piece and the preparation then read each of its 4,094 label entries at
  1,000 topics. *Decision:* `#regroupKey` returns whether the element is in
  another group than before, and the records of the folds are given again only
  then. The group of an element is the identifier of the labels its cone
  instances consumed. *Alternative:* the record at every change of a label
  entry of a member. *Measured:* an edit of a title of the middle topic takes
  11, 12 and 18 ms at 100, 1,000 and 2,000 topics, against 15, 48 and 89 ms.
  *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/crossref.test.ts`, "gives no record of
  the index of the rows by name when another writer writes the title of a topic,
  which no body reads". *If decided otherwise:* `#regroupKey` (question 399).
- **P83. An array of scalars that differs from the stored one at more than one
  position is written whole.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is
  no owner ruling. *The case:* the kept index stores its occupied keys as an
  array in the order the buckets came to exist. A topic whose name changes takes
  its key out of the middle and adds one at the end, and `put` in
  `Instance.#place` wrote each position behind the one that left with a record
  of its own: 500 of 521 records at 1,000 topics, and a preparation that is the
  number of records times the number of label entries. *Decision:* such an
  array is written whole, as an array of another length is: one write and one
  record (`shiftedScalars`). *Alternative:* no array of the occupied keys, which
  is the plan of question 379. *Measured:* 20 records at every size, the piece's
  own time 6, 34 and 68 ms and the preparation 9, 53 and 119 ms. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/kept-index.test.ts`, "gives one record of the
  occupied keys, and none of a position among them, when a key leaves the middle
  of them and another enters". *If decided otherwise:* `shiftedScalars`
  (question 401).
- **P84. The assembly of a `flatMap` whose bodies return the result of an inner
  per-element construct keeps its segments and splices the one that changed.**
  The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  the assembly of a `flatMap` over an array of references depended on each
  element's body and on the inner assembly each body returned, and
  `Instance.#reassemble` refused an entry with a dependency beside those of the
  elements, so a change of one topic's mentions formed every segment again and
  located every member: 1,003 positions read at 1,000 topics. *Decision:* where
  every body returned the assembled result of another per-element construct,
  the assembly keeps the length of each segment and its dependency on each
  inner assembly (`Rows.segments`), and a mark that names an element or its
  inner assembly puts the members of that segment in the place of those it had,
  as one splice. A change of the source array, and a `flatMap` whose body
  returns a stored array or writes one, are formed whole. *Alternative:* the
  whole assembly for every change. *Measured:* an edit of the mentions reads 4
  positions at every size. *Tests:* `exec/test/crossref.test.ts`, "forms the
  segment of the one topic whose mentions changed, among 1,000 topics as among
  10". *If decided otherwise:* `Rows.segments`.
- **P85. The sort by a key is the method `sortBy` with one key function,
  ascending, with texts ordered by their code units.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It replaces P71. *The case:*
  the `lift` `topicsByActivity` of the board `sorted-references`. *Decision:*
  `xs.sortBy((x) => key)`; a descending order is a negated numeric key. The plan
  holds a `Collection` whose `construct` is `sortBy`, with the key function as
  its body cone, observed as `value`, and the membership template of a
  `filter`: the `fold` of the key over every element joined with the source's
  membership. The order of keys is `compareSortKeys` of `exec/executor.ts`:
  numbers by value, texts by their code units, `false` before `true`; a number
  before a text before a boolean; `null`, `undefined` and `NaN` behind every
  other key; equal keys in the order of the source. Over an array of references
  a changed key is two splices and one evaluation of the body of the element
  that moved; over the result of another per-element construct the order is
  formed whole for each change. `base/api/index.ts` declares no `sortBy`, so a
  source that uses it does not run on today's runtime. On the board a topic
  whose key reads as `undefined` has a card behind every other, where the
  `lift` leaves it out. *Alternative:* the recognized comparator of P71; and
  `localeCompare` for texts, whose order follows the locale of the process.
  *Tests:* `tests/plan.rs`, `exec/test/sort-by.test.ts` and
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/sort-by.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* the
  arm of `Emitter::method`, `Rows.sortKeys` and `compareSortKeys` (question
  382).
- **P86. A `map` over a `sortBy` of an array of references has its rows as
  documents.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling.
  It extends P54. *The case:* the cards of `sorted-references`. *Decision:*
  `rowDocumentCollections` takes a `map` over a `sortBy` of an array of
  references as it takes one over a `filter` of one. The link at a position then
  has the fold of the keys and the row's document its own label. *Alternative:*
  rows in place, where each row stores the label of the order. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/sort-by.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* that
  arm of `rowDocumentCollections`.
- **P87. The two measured Topics boards declare the members of the namespace as
  cells.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The
  case:* the rows of `namesTable`, a `map` over the entries of a record of
  references, were in place on the boards, because the boards declared `names`
  as a record of unknown values, and the result document held three label
  entries for each topic below `namesTable`. *Decision:*
  `board-filing-order.tsx` declares the input of both boards as `BoardInput`,
  whose `names` is a record of `Writable<TopicDemand>` (`BoardNames`), where
  `main.tsx` declares a record of unknown values. `rowDocumentCollections` then
  takes the `map` over the entries of the record (P78), and the result document
  holds a link for each row. *Alternative:* the rows in place. *Measured:* 6
  label entries below `namesTable` at every size of the board. *Tests:* none of
  its own; the boards are measured. *If decided otherwise:* the input type of
  the two boards, which are on a local branch.
- **P88. Each bucket of a kept index is a document of its own, the stored index
  holds no array of its occupied keys, and the record of the buckets is written
  member by member.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner
  ruling. It carries out the plan of question 379 for the index. *The case:* a
  kept index was one record of the result document, with a bucket and a label
  entry for each key and an array of the occupied keys. A change of one member's
  key wrote the record of the buckets whole where a key left it and another
  entered, and the array of the occupied keys whole where a key left the middle
  of it (P83): a write as long as the index for a change of one member, in a
  result document of 2.0 MB at 1,000 topics. *Decision:*
  `bucketDocumentCollections` of `exec/row-documents.ts` names a `groupBy` or a
  `keyBy` written in no element body that the result keeps at a path through no
  element. For such an index `Instance.indexRecord` of `exec/executor.ts` gives
  `{ kind, mode, buckets }` and no `keys`; the occupied keys are the names of
  the members of `buckets`, in the order the buckets came to exist. The executor
  writes `buckets` member by member, and removes a bucket that emptied. The
  adapter stores the bucket of an encoded key in a document named by the
  document and the path of the record and by the key, with a link to it at the
  bucket's member (`BucketRecord`, `#bucketDocument` and `#writeBucket` of
  `runtime/runner/src/compiled/transactions.ts`). A second piece that is handed
  the stored index reads a bucket through the link. With `rows` at `in-place`
  the buckets stay in the result document. *Alternative:* the index as one
  record, as before; or the state document of `execution-and-storage.md` §6.3
  for the whole index. *Measured:* the result document at 1,000 topics is 0.81
  MB with 66 label entries at every size, and an edit of a `shortName` takes 20,
  35 and 389 ms at 100, 1,000 and 2,000 topics where it took 42, 275 and 969,
  the 389 ms holding a pause of the harness. *What it leaves:* `keys()` and
  `keyEntries()` are not built; the executor still forms the record of the index
  whole for each change; and the labels of a bucket document are P89, with the
  questions 405 to 408. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/kept-index.test.ts` and `crossref.test.ts`. *If
  decided otherwise:* `bucketDocumentCollections`, `Instance.indexRecord` and
  `#writeBucket`.
- **P89. A bucket document has the record of the index at a write at or above
  the record of the buckets, and the join of what its transaction read after
  that; a read of a bucket by the executor names the position of the link as one
  it went through.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner
  ruling. *The case:* three facts of the runtime, each found by a test. A read
  that follows a link consumes the label of the document the link leads to and
  nothing of the entries above the link in the document that holds it. The
  record of the index, instantiated for a write after the load, gives the clause
  of the member that changed and not the fold over every member. And a record of
  the plan has to name a path the transaction wrote, so the link of a bucket
  cannot be covered by a record at `buckets`. *Decision:* at a write at or above
  `buckets`, as the load makes it, each bucket document has the record of the
  index and stores the fold. A bucket document written after that is written
  under no record and stores the join of what its transaction read; the
  transaction reads the index at its own position in the result document
  (`kind`), so the join holds the entry of the index. For a read by the executor
  of a bucket at its path in the result document, the adapter names the position
  of the link as a position the read went through (`#crossedBucketLink`), and
  the label of the read joins what it consumes of the result document there with
  what it consumes of the bucket document. *Alternative:* the fold stored in
  every bucket document at each change of the membership, which is a write for
  each bucket. *What it leaves:* a suspected under-label of a bucket that the
  transaction does not write, an over-label of a bucket written after the load,
  and two label entries for each link to a bucket made after the load (questions
  405 to 408, deferred by the ruling Z88). Two assertions of `crossref.test.ts`
  on a read of `byName/buckets` expect five clauses where they expected four
  (question 411). *Tests:* `kept-index.test.ts` and `crossref.test.ts`. *If
  decided otherwise:* `#writeBucket` and `#crossedBucketLink`.
- **P90. A splice that shifts more than 16 positions of an array of row
  documents is one write of the array, under a read of the array.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a
  change of one sort key gives two splices of the assembly, and the adapter
  wrote every position behind each splice through the transaction: at 2,000
  topics 3,000 writes of a link for a move from the middle to the front, 34 ms
  of the step's 123 ms. *Decision:* a splice that changes the length and shifts
  more than 16 positions is written as the array of links the adapter holds
  (`SPLICE_AS_POSITIONS` of `transactions.ts`), and the transaction reads the
  array, so that the commit can send the difference as a splice where the server
  takes one. *Alternative:* a write for each position, as before; or a
  representation of an order that a move writes a bounded part of, which is not
  built because the reader of the order is the list of the children of a view
  node, an array, and the transaction of the runtime has no write of a splice.
  *Measured:* an edit of `lastActivityAt` on `sorted-references` takes 56 and 94
  ms at 1,000 and 2,000 topics in the median of three runs, where one run
  without the change had 55 and 123. The storage still reports one changed path
  for each position between the old place and the new. *What it leaves:* the
  step follows the board, the wire form of a move was not read, and the read of
  the array joins its label into the writes under no record (questions 410 and
  425). *Tests:* none of its own; the boards are measured. *If decided
  otherwise:* `SPLICE_AS_POSITIONS`.
- **P91. Nothing is read of the computed part of a body's argument at a path
  that an entry of `Body.reads` fills, and an entry that gives way reads no
  slot.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It
  carries out, in the executor, the first step of the plan of question 388, and
  a part of the plan of question 381. *The case:* `Host.invoke` of
  `exec/executor.ts` copied the computed part of the argument (`Host.pass`),
  which reads each reference in it, and then read each entry of `Body.reads`
  with `Host.slot` and put it at its path. A `lift` over an array of plain
  values in place read the array twice for a call. A `lift` that declares a
  record as a cell and reads one scalar of it as a value, as `backlinksOf` of
  `topic.tsx` does with the stored index and its `kind`, read the whole record
  with every link followed before the entry of the cell put a handle there: the
  first derivation of a new topic read the index, every row it links to and
  every topic those hold, and depended on all of it. *Decision:* `pass` gives
  nothing at a path that a `value` or an `identity` entry of `Body.reads` fills,
  and the slot of an `enumeration` entry is read only where the entry does not
  give way to what the argument holds. The emitter still writes the expression
  of the computed part, and nothing is read from it. *Alternative:* the emitter
  passes `$h.invoke` nothing at such a path, which changes every emitted
  fixture. *Measured:* an edit of one title in a `lift` over 100, 1,000 and
  10,000 plain values in place takes 0.56, 5.5 and 57 ms on the executor in
  memory where it took 1.0, 10.2 and 99; a create on Topics reads 283, 2,083 and
  4,083 positions where it read 801, 7,101 and 14,101. *What it leaves:*
  `Store.read` copies what it reads, and a transaction that runs a body reads
  less than it did, which the join of a write under no record then holds less of
  (question 409). *Tests:*
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/body-argument.test.ts` over
  `compare/fixtures/body-argument.tsx`. *If decided otherwise:* `Host.invoke`
  and `Host.pass`.
- **P92. A stored plain value that holds links is keyed by its content with each
  link as the address it names.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it
  is no owner ruling. It closes a defect of correctness and carries out the plan
  of question 380 for a stored array. *The case:* `Store.#keysOf` of
  `exec/store.ts` formed the key of each plain member of a stored array from the
  member read with every link followed. For a `map` over plain values generated
  from scratch that hold references, a write of a document that a reference
  leads to formed every key again from the changed content, and every row then
  held nothing; and for values that refer to documents that refer to each other
  the keying walked a graph as a tree, so that a fixture took five times as long
  for each four topics more. *Decision:* a member that holds links is keyed by
  its own content with each link as the address of what it names
  (`Store.#linksNamed`, `Store.addressOf`), and a member that holds none keeps
  the key it has. The keying reads no document a link leads to and registers the
  reads that find what each link names (`Position.own`). *Alternative:* the hash
  that follows every link, with the rows kept by another means. *What it
  changes:* the keys of stored plain values that hold links, and with them the
  identity of what is derived for each; the ruling on the salted hash of a plain
  value says nothing of a link inside the value. *What it leaves:*
  `Instance.#table` keys a plain value of an array that no document holds with
  every reference followed, and no fixture reaches it with a value that holds a
  reference. Its label side is question 400. *Tests:*
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/value-references.test.ts` over
  `compare/fixtures/value-references.tsx`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `Store.#keysOf`.
- **P100. A handle keeps the instance and the host in private fields, and the
  classes of what a function body is given are frozen where a compartment
  evaluator is made.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner
  ruling. It closes a defect of soundness. *The case:* `Handle` held the
  instance and the host of its cone in public members, and the crate's check
  accepts a member that the type of a handle does not declare, so a handler body
  of an accepted pattern, evaluated in the compartment, read the executor's
  store through `last.instance`. *Decision:* both are private fields of `Handle`
  (`Handle.refusingWrites` is the one use outside the class), and
  `compartmentEvaluator` freezes `Handle`, `Ref` and `StreamRef` with their
  prototypes. A body still reads `handle.target`. *What it leaves:* the check
  still accepts the undeclared member, and `$h` and `$rt` are confined by the
  check alone (question 386). *Alternative:* a membrane between the executor and
  value code, which copies or wraps each value for each call. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/value-code.test.ts`, the two cases on a handle.
  *If decided otherwise:* the private fields and `freezeHandedClasses` of
  `runtime/runner/src/compiled/value-code.ts`.
- **P101. The crate runs on load as its release binary in a child process,
  started from the realm that starts the piece.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* milestone 5 has the runtime
  compile on load with the crate in the compile worker. *Decision:*
  `PatternCompiler` of `runtime/runner/src/compiled/compile.deno.ts` writes the
  files of the program to a temporary directory, runs the binary there with
  `emit --accepted`, and removes the directory. It is not a WebAssembly build:
  the crate reads its modules with `std::fs` and has a binary, and a
  WebAssembly build needs a target, bindings for the file reads and a built
  artifact that something keeps current. It is not started from the compile
  worker (`ModuleCompileWorker`): the worker exists to take the type check and
  the emit off the thread of the realm, and a child process is off it already.
  With `cacheDir` the output is kept under the hash of the binary's bytes and
  the hash of the source. *Alternative:* a WebAssembly build in the compile
  worker. *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/compile.test.ts`,
  `base/pattern-compiler/compare/test/compile-on-load.test.ts` and
  `base/pattern-compiler/tests/emit_accepted.rs`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `PatternCompiler.compile`; the cache and the errors stay (questions 387 and
  389).
- **P102. A piece makes a compartment of its own, and a caller may share one
  evaluator among pieces.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* how many compartments the value code of a process
  runs in. *Decision:* `startCompiledPiece` makes one `compartmentEvaluator()`
  for a piece, 0.09 to 0.12 ms after the first of a process, and
  `CompiledPieceOptions.evaluate` takes one that a caller made. Sharing is
  admitted by two properties: the global object of the compartment is frozen,
  and a module's text is the body of a function, so one module leaves nothing in
  the compartment that another finds. *Alternative:* one compartment for each
  module, as today's bundles have. *Tests:* `value-code.test.ts`, a module that
  assigns to a global does not load. *If decided otherwise:* the default of
  `startCompiledPiece`.
- **P103. The globals of value code are those of a module of today's bundles
  without `__cfReg`, with the gated clock under a frame of a handler.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* what
  value code may name. *Decision:* the globals of
  `createModuleCompartmentGlobals` without the registrar of hoisted builder
  artifacts, which value code does not call. `CompiledPiece` runs each compiled
  handler under a frame of a handler with the time of the event, so the gated
  `Date` gives a handler the event's time to the second and the gated `Math` a
  random draw; the derivation and module scope run under no such frame, and the
  same calls throw there. Today's module verifier is not run on value code, as
  `language-subset.md` §3.4 has it. *Alternative:* a set of globals of the
  design's own. *Tests:* `value-code.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `valueCodeGlobals` of `value-code.ts` (question 402).

- **P110. A client writes the program of a pattern, in an entity named by its
  text, and the document named from the result document names that entity.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It replaces P133
  as to what a client writes, and closes a defect of soundness: with P133 the
  serving runtime evaluated value code that a client wrote. *The case:* how the
  serving runtime of a space learns which pattern a piece is of. *Decision:*
  `setUpCompiledPiece(runtime, tx, program, argument, resultCell)` of
  `runtime/runner/src/compiled/setup.ts` writes the program as JSON text, the
  files by name with the name of the main file and of the export, into an entity
  named by that text (`patternSourceDocumentOf`); the document
  `compiledPointerOf(result)` holds `{ source }`; and the argument document
  holds each cell as a link. The loader of `serveCompiledPieces` compiles the
  program with the compiler it was given (`ServeCompiledPiecesOptions.compile`),
  keeps what the compiler gave by the entity of the source, and evaluates the
  value code in a compartment. It evaluates no artifact it finds stored.
  *Alternative:* the client writes the artifact, as P133 had it; or a meta field
  of the result document in the place of the pointer, which needs a member of
  the closed set `META_FIELDS`. *What the specification asks that is not met*
  (`scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §10.5): the compile is awaited inside the
  loop's start of the piece, the compiled pattern is not stored as a document of
  the space with the integrity of compiled output, and a build of the compiler
  is no part of the identity a piece names. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/compiled-serving.test.ts`, the cases under "the
  compiled pattern of a piece", and
  `base/pattern-compiler/compare/test/serving-compile.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* `setup.ts` and the loader (questions 417 and 434).
- **P111. The serving runtime writes why it started no piece into a document
  named from the result document.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it
  is no owner ruling. *The case:* a client that set a piece up has to learn that
  the serving runtime refused it. *Decision:* where the document names no
  source, the source is no program, or the compiler rejects, the loader writes
  `{ reason }` into the document `compiledFailureOf(result)`, in a transaction
  stamped as a derivation with no acting principal, starts nothing, and returns
  to the loop that the piece is not served. The reason of a refused source is
  the text of the compiler's diagnostics. It is written once: a later demand
  finds the compile kept and the reason stored. *Alternative:* no stored reason,
  and a log of the server. *Tests:* `compiled-serving.test.ts`, the second and
  the third case under "the compiled pattern of a piece". *If decided
  otherwise:* `refuse` of `serving.ts` (question 419).
- **P112. A host keeps the instance in a private field, and the compartment
  evaluator freezes every class of the executor whose instances value code is
  handed, makes or catches.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no
  owner ruling. It extends P100 and closes two defects of soundness. *The case:*
  `Host`, the object every value function is called with as `$h` and that
  `$rt.nohost` holds, kept its instance in the public member `instance`, so
  `$rt.nohost.instance.store` was the store of the executor. And the evaluator
  froze `Handle`, `Ref` and `StreamRef` alone, so a body that assigned to a
  method of the prototype of the host replaced it for every piece of the
  process. Both needed a text that names `$rt` or `$h`, which the crate's check
  refuses. *Decision:* the instance is a private field of `Host`. The executor
  lists the classes (`HANDED_CLASSES`: `Unsupported`, `Assembled`, `Index`,
  `IndexHandle`, `Thunk`, `ReadsFailure`, `Handle`, `Host` and `NoHost`), and
  `compartmentEvaluator` freezes each with its prototype, with `Ref`,
  `StreamRef`, `StreamMarker`, `MissingKey` and `ComputedOutput` of the store.
  *Alternative:* a membrane between the executor and value code. *What it
  leaves:* `$rt` and `$h` are objects whose methods a text that names them can
  call, each on the instance the code belongs to; and the classes are frozen for
  the whole process when the first evaluator is made (questions 386 and 423).
  *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/value-code.test.ts`, three cases. *If
  decided otherwise:* `HANDED_CLASSES` and `freezeHandedClasses` of
  `value-code.ts`.
- **P113. The sources of a piece are the documents its derivation reads and does
  not derive, as the adapter observes them.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* what a resume compares with the
  storage to know that a stored result is current. *Decision:* a piece keeps one
  document, named from its result document (`basisDocumentOf` of
  `runtime/runner/src/compiled/basis.ts`), in the form of
  `scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §10.4 with the piece as the unit. Its sources
  are: a document that exists outside the executor and that the executor read;
  the argument document; a document that a transaction of the executor other
  than a derivation wrote; a place of the executor's own that was read while the
  storage held no document of it; a document another writer changed and the
  executor took the change of; and the document of the counts of P132. A
  document the derivation alone writes is no source. The adapter tells the piece
  of each through `SourceObserver`. The basis also lists the documents the
  executor made that are no rows, and the entities of the streams.
  *Alternative:* rows of a cone instance, which §10.4 specifies and which is the
  plan of question 430. *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/basis.test.ts`.
  *If decided otherwise:* `PieceBasis` of `basis.ts` (questions 420 and 430).
- **P114. The basis records, for a source, the sequence number of the replica's
  confirmed view at a derivation with no write of the piece to it unconfirmed.**
  The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  which number names what a derivation saw of a source. *Decision:*
  `ISpaceReplica.confirmedDocumentSeq` of the document when such a derivation
  ran. The executor holds every source in memory and takes each change of
  another writer when the replica applies it, so that number names what the
  derivation saw, and the source is unchanged while its head is that number. A
  source in another space is recorded as never current. *Alternative:* the hash
  of the content of the source, which is work that follows the size of an array
  a handler appends to. *Tests:* `basis.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `PieceBasis`.
- **P115. A source the piece wrote and the replica has not confirmed is listed
  as recent, read whole by the transaction that writes the basis, and unchanged
  while its head is not behind the head of the basis.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a piece cannot know
  the number its own commit will give a document; in a serving runtime the
  handler's transaction and the derivation's are sealed into one wave and get
  one number, after both ran. *Decision:* the basis has a list `recent` of such
  sources. The transaction that writes the basis reads each of them whole, so
  that its commit depends on what the document holds; every write of the basis
  names all of them again; and a counter `revision` makes every write a change.
  When a later derivation finds the commit confirmed, the source gets its number
  and leaves the list. *It rests on an assumption:* a transaction that read a
  document whole is refused where the document changed before its commit, for a
  commit of a client and for a contribution to a wave; no test covers a wave
  (question 429). *Alternatives:* a second commit after each event that records
  the number, one more wave for each event; the hash of the content; or rows the
  memory server writes inside the store transaction of the wave, which §10.4
  specifies and which replaces the list. *Tests:* `basis.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* `PieceBasis` (question 421).
- **P116. A derivation writes the basis where its transaction has other writes
  or a transaction of the piece wrote a source since, and a change by another
  writer that the derivation wrote nothing for writes nothing.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* when
  the document of the basis is written. *Decision:* by a transaction of the
  derivation alone, after `settle()`: at the load, at a resume, and in a
  derivation whose transaction has other writes or behind which a transaction of
  the piece wrote a source. A commit of a handed transaction that stores a label
  alone moved the head of a document, so the adapter tells the piece of each
  document such a commit changed, and the derivation runs once more and records
  it. A change by another writer of a field that no cone reads leaves the basis
  one number behind, and until the next write of the basis a resume finds that
  piece stale. A transaction whose commit is refused, or taken back after a
  rejected wave, takes its write of the basis with it, and the piece then writes
  the document whole. *Alternative:* a write of the basis in every derivation,
  which is a commit for a change that wrote nothing. *Tests:* `basis.test.ts`;
  the corpus with `--resume`, where five modules were found stale at every
  resume before a commit that stores a label counted as a write. *If decided
  otherwise:* `PieceBasis`.
- **P117. A piece whose basis matches the storage runs nothing until an event or
  a change of a source wakes it, and the loader of a serving runtime is told
  whether an event waits.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* a serving loop that takes a space over. *Decision:*
  `resumeCompiledPieceFromBasis` of `runtime/runner/src/compiled/resume.ts`
  reads the document of the basis, the documents of its parts and one document
  for each source, under a schema with which the sync follows no link, and
  compares the identity of the compiled pattern and then `basisMatches`. Where
  they match, no `Instance` is made, no value code is loaded and nothing is
  committed; the returned `ResumedPiece` wakes at a commit that changes a
  document the basis names, and its caller wakes it before an event.
  `ensureVerdict` passes the loader whether an event waits
  (`EnsurePieceOptions.forEvent`): a demand finds the piece served and reads
  what is stored, and an event wakes it. Where they do not match, and at a wake,
  the resume of P130 runs. *Alternative:* the resume of P130 for every piece a
  loop reaches. *Measured:* a takeover at 10,000 rows evaluates nothing and
  reads 10,268 documents, and a client reads the last row in 1.7 s, where
  today's piece takes 47 s; the first event then takes 3.5 s. *Tests:*
  `basis.test.ts` and two cases of `compiled-serving.test.ts`. *If decided
  otherwise:* the loader's choice in `serving.ts` (questions 430 and 431).
- **P118. The load of a piece on a serving runtime brings its empty result
  document without what it links to.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23;
  it is no owner ruling. *The case:* the loader brought the documents of a piece
  under a schema that follows every link, the empty result document among them,
  so the serving session kept a query that the memory server walked over every
  row link at each append. *Decision:* `syncCompiledPiece` with `rows` false.
  *Measured:* an append at 1,000 rows went from 102 to 76 ms in one run each,
  and the load from 730 to 530 ms. *What it leaves:* a piece that is woken after
  a resume brings its rows with such a query, since the runtime offers no sync
  that follows links once and keeps no query. *If decided otherwise:* that
  argument of `syncCompiledPiece` (question 433).
- **P119. A resumed runtime enrolls a document of the piece as a store the
  instance owns with its first write of it, and brings by name the documents the
  basis lists as made by the piece.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23;
  it is no owner ruling. It closes two defects of soundness of a resume. *The
  case:* the adapter enrolls a document in the transaction that first writes it,
  and the runtime keeps the enrollment in memory, so a second runtime's write
  was measured for writer-fit and refused. And a document the result links to by
  no link a sync follows, an output kept in a document of its own or the entity
  of a stream held by a row stored in place, was read as absent and made again,
  and the commit conflicted with the stored document. *Decision:* a resumed
  adapter enrolls each document it holds from the run before with its first
  write of it; the basis lists the documents the piece made, and a resume brings
