  each. A place the resumed executor finds no document of is a source of the
  basis, so the next resume brings it first. *What it leaves:* the list follows
  the number of rows where each row has a stream or a document of its own, and
  the name of a document is taken as proof that the piece made it (questions 422
  and 431). *Tests:* the corpus with `--resume`
  (`examples/cfc-exchange-rules/witnessed-chain.tsx` and
  `showcase/wordsearch/play.tsx` pass with it) and
  `compare/test/resume-corpus.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* the enrollment
  in `transactions.ts` and the list `documents` of the basis.
- **P120. The numbers of the sources of a basis are spread over 256 documents by
  a hash of the identifier of the source.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* with every number in the
  document of the basis, a list of 10,000 references gave a document of 10,000
  entries of which each event writes two or three paths, and a write of one path
  of a document costs the replica, the server and the commit work that follows
  the size of the document: a rename under server execution at 10,000 rows took
  62 ms with that basis and 29 ms with none, in one run each. *Decision:* the
  number of a source is in the document of a part (`basisPartOf`), and the
  document of the basis names the parts that exist. A resume reads the documents
  of the parts beside the sources. *Alternative:* one document. *Measured:* a
  rename takes 30 to 36 ms in four runs. *What it leaves:* the list of the
  documents the piece made is in the one document, and after a refused commit
  the piece writes every part again (question 431). *If decided otherwise:*
  `PARTS` and `basisPartOf` of `basis.ts`.
- **P130. A resume that derives evaluates the first derivation again and writes
  the paths that differ, with no record of the plan.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. With P117 it is what runs for a
  piece whose basis does not match the storage, and at a wake. *The case:* a
  runtime that holds nothing of a piece starts it from what is stored.
  *Decision:* `resumeCompiledPiece` of `resume.ts` brings every document of the
  piece and of its inputs (`syncCompiledPiece`), and the resumed instance
  evaluates the first derivation again against the stored argument and the
  stored state, in one transaction; a state cell whose document the storage
  holds is given neither its first value nor its default (the `Instance` option
  `resume`). A change that writes what the storage holds is no write: the
  runtime's transaction logs no attempt for it, and the adapter gives no record
  and does not count the path as written. A path whose value differs is written
  with no record of the plan, so the runtime labels it with the join of what the
  transaction read. The records are left out because a record names positions as
  written or staged that a resume did not write, and the preparation refuses
  those (`requireWritten` of `runtime/runner/src/cfc/plan-labels.ts`).
  *Alternative:* the record of each path that was written, with bindings to
  stored positions alone, which needs the adapter to tell, for each change,
  which of its targets the transaction wrote. *What it leaves:* the reads are of
  the whole board in one transaction, and where inputs changed a reader observes
  all differences at once (questions 412, 413 and 430). *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/resume.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `resumeCompiledPiece` and `RuntimeTransactions.change`.
- **P131. Each document the executor makes carries the `result` link to the
  result document.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner
  ruling. It closes a defect of a resume. *The case:* a link to a document the
  executor made and a link to an input are both stored as links to an entity,
  and the process that made a document knows which is which from a table in
  memory. A second process read every link as one to an input, so a member a
  handler had pushed got another key and another row document. *Decision:* the
  adapter writes the `result` link where it creates a document, a row document
  or the entity of a stream (`#linkToResult`), as the runner writes it onto the
  cells a piece owns, and a resumed adapter reads it to tell the two apart
  (`#heldDocumentOf`). The serving loop finds the piece of a document by the
  same link. *Alternative:* the name of the document alone. *Tests:*
  `resume.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* `#linkToResult` (question 415).
- **P132. The counts that name the runs of handlers and the documents handlers
  make are kept in a document of the piece.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. It closes a defect of soundness. *The
  case:* the executor names the run of a handler by the number of events the
  process handled, and a document a body makes with no cause of its own by the
  number of such documents (`#bindEvent`, `#fresh`). Both began at zero in a
  second process, so a handler after a resume gave a new member the name of a
  member an earlier run had made and overwrote it. *Decision:* the counts are
  kept in a document of the piece (`Instance.minted`,
  `RuntimeTransactions.writeMinted`), written in the transaction that advances
  them, and a resume goes on from them. That is one more document written by
  each event. *Alternative:* the run of a handler named by the identity of its
  event in the stream, which the serving loop has and the scheduler's handler is
  not given; it would make the names the same on a client that speculates.
  *Tests:* `resume.test.ts`, "gives, for an event sent after the resume, the
  values the first runtime gives". *If decided otherwise:* `writeMinted`
  (question 414).
- **P133. A document named from the result document names the compiled pattern
  of a piece.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling.
  Replaced by P110 as to what the named document holds: it held the artifact as
  text, which a client wrote. What stands is the pointer: a document named from
  the result document (`compiledPointerOf`) and no meta field, because the set
  of meta fields is closed (`META_FIELDS` of `meta-seam.ts`) and a new one is a
  decision for the runtime. *If decided otherwise:* `compiledPointerOf` of
  `setup.ts`.
- **P134. The load of a piece on a serving runtime is one transaction of a wave,
  stamped as a derivation with no acting principal.** The coordinator's decision
  of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a transaction that the loop
  did not stamp is refused at the seal ("unstamped transaction sealed into a
  wave"), and the transactions that a bounded load commits by itself are ones
  the wave has no run for. *Decision:* the loader stamps the transaction of the
  load as a derivation with no acting principal (`stampWaveRunContext`) and
  starts the piece with `loadRows` at `Infinity`. It does not wait for the
  outcome of the commit, which the wave settles after the cycle the load runs
  in. *Alternative:* a load that spans cycles, or rows committed ahead of the
  wave, which are the two plans of question 432. *What it leaves:* a reader sees
  nothing of the piece until the whole load committed, and the load over-labels
  what is bound through the argument (question 375). *Tests:*
  `compiled-serving.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* the loader's start in
  `serving.ts` (questions 416 and 432).
- **P135. The replica's revert of a transaction that had settled is a refused
  commit of the piece.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no
  owner ruling. It closes a defect of soundness. *The case:* a transaction
  sealed into a wave settles with no error before the wave commits; where the
  wave is then rejected, the replica takes the writes back and the loop queues
  the event again. The piece heard of a refused commit only through the outcome
  of the commit, so the executor stayed ahead of the storage and the handler ran
  again on top of its own first run: a count of 12 where 3 events had been sent.
  *Decision:* the adapter takes the replica's `revert` of a transaction it
  handed, where that transaction had settled without an error, as a refused
  commit (`Handed.settled`), and the piece restores the documents the
  transaction wrote from the storage (`Instance.restore`) before the event is
  handled again. `Instance.restore` keeps what the place of a state cell was
  declared as. *Alternative:* the withdrawal of the one derived write, as
  `scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §5.5 has it. *What it leaves:* the restore
  follows the size of the result, and a wave that holds the transactions of two
  pieces restores each (question 418). *Tests:* `compiled-serving.test.ts`, the
  case of an event whose wave is rejected. *If decided otherwise:* the
  subscription of `RuntimeTransactions`.
- **P136. A client under server execution runs nothing of a compiled piece.**
  The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-22; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  what a client does with a piece its serving runtime runs. *Decision:* a client
  sets the piece up (P110) and commits only the append of an event; `setup.ts`
  imports none of the executor. Today's client tries to run the handler of each
  event it sends, finds none, and logs "Event dropped: no handler registered";
  the event is appended all the same. *Alternative:* client speculation, as
  `scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §11 has it, which needs the compiled pattern
  delivered to clients. *Measured:* a client's own event reaches it in the time
  it reaches a second client, 16 to 31 ms for a rename at 100 to 10,000 rows,
  where today's sender shows its speculation in 4 to 10 ms. *Tests:*
  `compiled-serving.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* a client that starts the
  piece as well.
- **P140. A change of the source of a `flatMap` whose segments are kept takes
  out the segments of the elements that left and forms those of the elements
  that entered.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner
  ruling. It extends P84. *The case:* a `flatMap` over an array of references
  whose bodies return the result of an inner per-element construct was formed
  whole when the source array changed, so an append of one topic formed the
  segment of every topic and located every member of the array. *Decision:*
  `Instance.#reassemble` of `exec/executor.ts` applies the splices of the source
  to the kept segments: the lengths, the dependencies on the inner assemblies,
  the members and the values of the elements that left are taken out, and the
  segment of each element that entered is formed and put at its place. A
  `flatMap` over an empty source keeps no segments and is formed whole at its
  first element. *Measured:* a create at 1,000 topics reads 1,082 positions
  where it read 2,083. *Tests:*
  `base/pattern-compiler/exec/test/crossref.test.ts`, two cases. *If decided
  otherwise:* the branch of `#reassemble` for a change of the source.
- **P141. An `enumeration` or a `shape` entry of a handler's state that gives
  way to a handle is read with no link of a child followed.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* `Instance.#attempt`
  read each slot of a handler's state that does not observe `identity` with
  every link followed. A handler that reads `Object.keys(names.get() ?? {})` has
  an `enumeration` entry at the path of the handle `names`, and the read of that
  entry followed the link of each member of the record into each member's
  document, before the body read the record through its handle under its
  declared type, which follows none. *Decision:* the entry is read under a
  schema that types each child as unknown (`CHILDREN_UNREAD`), where it gives
  way to a handle the state holds at or above its path (`Instance.gives`). The
  slot is bound to the positions of the container. *What it leaves:* the
  transaction reads fewer documents, so the join of what it read holds less
  (question 440). *Tests:* `exec/test/handler-enumeration.test.ts` over
  `compare/fixtures/handler-enumeration.tsx`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `CHILDREN_UNREAD` in `#attempt`.
- **P142. A row whose value holds what `lookup` gave for a kept index with
  buckets as documents stores a link to the position of the bucket, with a
  record under which the output of the index has no label.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It builds, for such rows, what
  P69 designed. *The case:* a row of a keyed join that holds its bucket held the
  membership of the index in its label, so each row was given its record again
  when a member with a label of its own entered the source: 1,000 of 1,102
  records of a create at 1,000 topics. *Decision:* for a row of a per-element
  construct whose value holds what `lookup` gave, as it gave it, for an index of
  the same instance that the result keeps with its buckets as documents,
  `Instance.#formOf` stores a reference to the position of the bucket below the
  record `buckets` of the kept index. `Instance.#heldByReference` gives the
  record of the row with the inputs of the output of the index replaced by
  inputs under which that output has no label, so the label stored at the row's
  position is that of the key, and a change of the membership gives no record of
  the row. A read through the link reads the result document at the position of
  the bucket, below the entry of the index, and then the bucket's document. A
  row whose key has no bucket holds an empty array in place under the record it
  had. A row derived from its bucket holds no bucket and is stored as the result
  of another per-element construct. *Alternative:* a reference for a key with no
  bucket as well, which would read as `undefined` through the runtime where the
  executor gives an empty array. *What it leaves:* questions 394, 439 and 442.
  *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/bucket-reference.test.ts`, seven cases.
  *If decided otherwise:* `#heldByReference` and `bucketPlaces`.
- **P143. Where a bucket of a kept index with buckets as documents changed, the
  record of the index is given again at the path of the index.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a
  change of a bucket wrote the record of the index at the leaves the comparison
  found unchanged, `kind` and `mode`, which a read of a bucket does not pass, so
  the entry above the buckets did not hold the membership as it is. *Decision:*
  `Instance.#storeIndex` gives the record of the index at the path of the index
  as a record that forms the label alone (`#unchangedOutput`). *What it costs:*
  the record stores a label entry of the result document, so an edit of the
  mentions that changes a bucket writes that document, 1.14 MB at 1,000 topics,
  where it wrote four small documents. *Tests:* `bucket-reference.test.ts`, the
  last case. *If decided otherwise:* `#storeIndex` (question 442).
- **P144. The result holds a kept index with buckets as documents by reference,
  and the buckets that changed are stored by themselves.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* the result of an
  instance held such an index whole, so a change of one bucket evaluated the
  result again, formed the record of every bucket, formed its canonical text and
  compared each bucket with what the store held. *Decision:* the result holds
  the reference to the index. `Instance.#indexForm` stores the index whole the
  first time it stands at its path, and afterwards `Instance.#storeIndex` writes
  the buckets that a change of the assembly touched (`Index.changed`) and
  removes those that emptied. An index that is formed again whole is stored
  whole, each bucket compared. *Measured:* the piece's own time in an edit of a
  `shortName` is 3 to 5 ms at every size, where it was 5, 12 and 16 ms. *Tests:*
  `exec/test/bucket-documents.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* `#indexForm`.
- **P145. The rows of the pivot of the two measured Topics boards hold the pairs
  of their bucket, and the boards keep the index of the pairs.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It is a choice of
  the boards on the measurement branch and none of the design. *Decision:* a row
  of the pivot holds `mentionedBy: byMentioned.lookup(topic)`, the pairs, where
  it held the topics that mention, the result keeps the index of the pairs as
  `mentionIndex`, and `backlinksOf` of `topic.tsx` reads `from` of each pair.
  *What it costs:* the result document holds one more record of links, 1.14 MB
  at 1,000 topics where it was 0.84 MB, and the load writes one more document
  for each topic that is mentioned. Today's type check refuses `topic.tsx` in
  this form. *Tests:* the facts the harness reads of the board at 100 topics
  equal those of the form before. *If decided otherwise:* the two boards and
  `topic.tsx` on `claude/compiled-pattern-topics-runs`.
- **P146. An array of row documents that a transaction splices so that positions
  shift is written once, when the transaction ends, from one link kept for each
  row.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It
  stands on P90. *The case:* a change of one sort key gives two changes of the
  array of row documents, and the adapter wrote the array of links whole for
  each and built the link of every position each time: 38 of the piece's own 48
  ms of a move at 2,000 topics. *Decision:* `RuntimeTransactions` keeps the
  identifier and the link of the document of each row by its key
  (`RowArray.ids`, `RowArray.links`) and writes an array whose positions shifted
  once, when the transaction ends (`#writeSplicedArrays`); the rows that entered
  are written when their change arrives. *Alternative, tried:* the positions
  between the first and the last that differ written one by one, which the
  commit sends as marked splices and the preparation refuses, since the record
  of the array then names a path the transaction did not write (question 441).
  *Tests:* `runtime/runner/test/compiled/sorted-rows.test.ts`, five cases,
  written after the code. *If decided otherwise:* `#writeSplicedArrays`.
- **P150. Value code is handed the members of a record in the order of the
  storage.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It
  builds P1 for the executor on the runner path and closes a finding of
  soundness (question 426). *The case:* the JSON codec writes a record with its
  names in the order of their UTF-8 bytes, so a process that reads a document
  from the storage holds each record in that order, and the process that wrote
  it holds it as written. Value code observed both, and a piece that the basis
  found current could hold a result that a fresh derivation does not give.
  *Decision:* `membersInOrder` of `exec/store.ts` gives the names of a record
  with the array indexes first, in the order of the numbers, and the others by
  their UTF-8 bytes. `Store.#copy` builds the copy of a stored record from the
  names in that order, and `Host.v` does the same for a record that one
  computation made and another reads. *What it changes for an author:* `{ title,
  tags }` is read as `{ tags, title }`, and a `map` over the entries of a record
  gives its rows in that order. *Alternative:* the order as written, kept in
  storage, which the codec does not keep. *What it leaves:* `Store.write` and
  `Store.put` compare by a text that holds the order, and the order in which an
  index gives its keys was not examined. *Tests:*
  `exec/test/member-order.test.ts`, five cases, and
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/member-order.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `membersInOrder` (question 450).
- **P151. An event a handler of a compiled piece sends is sent with `Cell.send`
  on the cell of its stream in the handler's transaction.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It closes a finding of
  soundness (question 427) and changes what P52 says of a handler's send. *The
  case:* the piece queued what a handler sent with the scheduler of the process,
  so a serving loop that stopped between the handler's commit and the handling
  of the event lost it. *Decision:* the handler of the scheduler that runs a
  compiled handler sends each such event with `Cell.send` on the cell of the
  entity that holds the stream's marker, bound to the transaction the scheduler
  gave the handler (`CompiledPiece.#registerStream`). On a serving runtime the
  entry is written into the document of the entries of the stream in that
  transaction, with the acting principal of the run as `firedAt`, and is stored
  and withdrawn with what the handler wrote; on any other runtime the event is
  one of the scheduler's queue. *Tests:* `compiled-serving.test.ts`, two cases
  over `compare/fixtures/relay.tsx`, and `handler-send.test.ts`. *What the tests
  do not show:* a loop that the deadline of a wave cuts between the two handlers
  by itself. *If decided otherwise:* `#registerStream` (question 447).
- **P152. The instances the handlers of a piece made are listed in the document
  of the counts, and a resume starts each before the first derivation of the
  piece.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It
  closes a finding of soundness (question 428). *The case:* no body makes an
  instance of a handler's run again, since the name of a run is formed from the
  count of the events handled, so such an instance had no handler and no
  derivation after a resume. *Decision:* `Instance.madeByHandlers` gives each
  instance a handler made that exists, by its identifier with the identity of
  its pattern; `CompiledPiece.#keepMinted` writes the list into the document of
  the counts (P132), as the member `made`, in the transaction in which it
  changed; and a resume reads the list, finds the artifact of each by the
  identity, and has the root make each with the argument the storage holds for
  it. This is the instances document of `execution-and-storage.md` §2.8 with the
  run and the ordinal left out. *What it leaves:* the list is written whole when
  it changes, every listed instance is started at a wake, and an instance that
  was re-keyed is listed under the identifier its documents have. *Tests:*
  `made-instance-resume.test.ts` over `compare/fixtures/made-counter.tsx`. *If
  decided otherwise:* `#keepMinted` (questions 448 and 449).
- **P153. A wake brings the result document and what it links to one document at
  a time, and keeps no query that follows the links of the result.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It does for the
  wake what P118 does for the load. *The case:* a wake brought the result
  document with a sync under a schema that declares no structure, which stays a
  query of the session, and on a serving runtime that reads over a session the
  memory server walked that query again at each commit of the wake: the first
  event after a takeover took 18 s at 1,000 topics. *Decision:* `bringReached`
  of `resume.ts` brings the result document and what a link leads to from it, at
  any depth, each document once and each by a sync of that one document under a
  schema that follows no link; the inputs are brought with the query that
  follows links. *Tests:* none of its own; the tests of the resume and of the
  serving loop pass with it. *If decided otherwise:* `bringReached` (question
  451).
- **P170. The freeze of module data and the hardening of functions are functions
  of the executor that the emitted text calls, under every evaluator.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  `language-subset.md` §3.3 says the compiler emits the freeze of each constant
  of frozen data and the hardening of each authored function, and the emitter
  wrote neither. *Decision:* the emitter wraps the initializer of each `const`
  of module scope in `$rt.fn(...)` or `$rt.data(...)`, names each declared
  function to `$rt.fn` in the first line of the text, and wraps a default
  export; `freezeModuleData` and `hardenFunction` of `exec/frozen.ts` do the
  work, under `new Function` as in the compartment. The executor freezes the
  exports of a module, the record imported from `commonfabric` with its
  functions, and each function of `$rt`. *Alternative:* a freeze by the
  evaluator, which has the text and not its bindings. *What it leaves:* the
  freeze exists twice, beside `freezeVerifiedPlainData` of the runner's sandbox.
  *Tests:* `tests/emit.rs` and
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/module-freeze.test.ts`, seventeen writes. *If
  decided otherwise:* `frozen_code` of `src/emit.rs`.
- **P171. What a handle and an index handle name is in private fields, and a
  handle, a reference and a stream reference are frozen when made.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It closes a
  finding of soundness and extends P100. *The case:* a body of an accepted
  source set a member of `handle.declared`, a schema object of the artifact that
  every piece of the source in the process reads under, and could set
  `handle.target` and write through the handle to another position. *Decision:*
  `target`, `slot`, `below`, `declared` and `fixed` of `Handle`, and the context
  of `IndexHandle`, are private fields that the executor reads with `partsOf`,
  `targetOf` and `indexPartsOf`. *Tests:* `module-freeze.test.ts`; the case of a
  handle did not fail first. *If decided otherwise:* `Handle` of
  `exec/executor.ts`.
- **P172. A declaration whose name begins with `$` is refused, under
  `stdlib:unsupported-member` until the document has an identifier for it.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It closes a
  finding of soundness. *The case:* a source that declares `const $h =
  ["plain"]` at module scope and reads `$h.at(0)` in a function of the reactive
  tier was accepted, and the emitted text read the host of the call there, and
  through it any slot of the plan. *Decision:* `Checker::reserved_names` of
  `src/check/mod.rs` refuses every declaration of a module whose name begins
  with `$`. With it, `TypedRules::handle_member` refuses a member of a handle
  that `language-subset.md` §4.7 does not list and a write to a listed one,
  under `cell:unsupported-method`. *What the document needs:* a rule for
  reserved names and an identifier in §10 (question 390). *Tests:*
  `tests/reserved_names.rs` and `tests/handle_members.rs`. *If decided
  otherwise:* the identifier alone.
- **P173. A piece started through `Runtime.run` is marked in storage as
  `setUpCompiledPiece` marks one.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it
  is no owner ruling. *The case:* which stored form says that a piece is
  compiled, for a runtime that starts the piece itself. *Decision:* the result
  document names no pattern identity, the document `compiledPointerOf(result)`
  holds the entity of the program, and that entity holds the program as text
  (P110); `Runner.run` writes the three in the transaction of the start. One
  form serves a client under server execution and a runtime that starts the
  piece itself. *Alternative:* a transaction of its own for the mark (question
  445). *Tests:* `compare/test/runtime-run.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `run` of `runtime/runner/src/compiled/run.ts`.
- **P174. The pattern a compiled piece names is the entity of its program
  text.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It
  answers the second decision of question 387, provisionally. *Decision:* the
  entity is named by the text of the program: the files, the main file and the
  export. No identity of today's compile is stored, and no compiler build; the
  identity a plan begins with is derived from the program at each compile.
  *Alternative:* the hash of the `CompiledPattern` record, as
  `scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §10.5 has it, which makes a build of the
  compiler part of the identity. *If decided otherwise:*
  `patternSourceDocumentOf` and the basis's comparison of `Plan.patterns[0]`.
- **P175. A resume whose program is no longer accepted is refused, with the
  reason stored, and does not fall back.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* a piece was started compiled,
  and the compiler that resumes it refuses its program. *Decision:* the loader
  stores the reason (`compiledFailureOf`, P111), starts nothing, and the stored
  result stays as it is. *Alternative:* today's path, which reads none of the
  documents the executor wrote for the piece and names its state cells
  otherwise, so the pattern would run from its argument with its state lost.
  Moving a piece between the two paths is a migration and is not built. *Tests:*
  `runtime-run.test.ts`, the last case. *If decided otherwise:* the loader of
  `serving.ts`.
- **P176. A program that the crate refuses, or whose plan requests `wish` or an
  effect, runs on today's path, with the reason logged.** The coordinator's
  decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It answers the first decision
  of question 387, provisionally, for a start. *The case:* `Runtime.run` of a
  program under the option. *Decision:* `prepare` keeps what the compiler
  rejected with, logs the warning `pattern-not-compiled` with the main file and
  the diagnostics, calls `fellBack`, and `run` returns false, so `Runner.run`
  goes on as without the option. A plan with a `wish` or an effect falls back
  because nothing answers a request of a compiled piece outside the executor's
  harness. An absent binary is no refusal: the compile rejects. *Measured:* of
  307 corpus modules that export a pattern, 103 run on today's path.
  *Alternative:* a refusal of the piece, as the serving loader does for a source
  a client wrote. *Tests:* `runtime-run.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `prepare` of `run.ts` (question 468).
- **P177. The compile has a bound on its output and a signal, and none on its
  time.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The
  case:* the child process was awaited with a call that holds all it prints.
  *Decision:* the two streams are read as they arrive (`readBounded`); a stream
  that holds more than `maxOutputBytes`, 256 MB unless given, has the child
  stopped and the compile rejects with `PatternCompilerOutputError`; a caller
  stops a compile with the `signal` it gives. The repository refuses a timeout
  as an upper bound on work that would have completed. *Tests:*
  `runtime/runner/test/compiled/compile.test.ts`; no test stops a compile by its
  signal. *If decided otherwise:* a deadline in `compile.deno.ts`.
- **P178. One compile of a source at a time within one compiler, and no claim
  between processes.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner
  ruling. *Decision:* a compile of a source whose compile is under way in the
  same `PatternCompiler` waits for that one. Two compilers of one process, or
  two processes, may both run the binary for one source; they write the same
  text under two names and rename. The first compile of a compiler with a cache
  directory removes the trees of other binaries. *Alternative:* a claim between
  processes, which needs a wait on another process's file: a poll, or a lock the
  shared compile cache has and this cache does not. *Tests:* `compile.test.ts`.
  *If decided otherwise:* the cache of `compile.deno.ts`.
- **P179. The keys of a whole read of an array without links are kept from the
  second such read on.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* a read of an array of plain values in place hashed
  every member at each read, about 40% of the read of 10,000 records, since the
  keys formed from the copies of a read were never kept. *Decision:* the copies
  of a read that left no member out, of an array no position of which is or
  holds a link, are what the store reads at those positions itself, so the keys
  formed from them are kept as `KeyState` and brought up to date at each write.
  From the second read and not the first: kept from the first, a `map` over
  plain values in place paid 8 to 10% at the load of 1,000 rows on the runner
  path. *Measured:* an edit under a `lift` over the whole array of 10,000 rows
  takes 27 ms where it took 70. *Tests:* `exec/test/store-read.test.ts`, four
  cases. *If decided otherwise:* `Store.#copy` (question 446).
- **P190. The walk of a type gives up at 24 steps.** The coordinator's decision
  of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:* `typed_at` of
  `src/declared.rs` returned no type past 12 steps from an expression to the
  declaration that types it, which left a type parameter unbound in
  `commitAttach` of FabriChat. *Decision:* 24. It is a limit of depth and no
  guard against a cycle, so a type still depends on how deeply its initializer
  is nested. *Alternative:* a guard against a cycle with no limit of depth.
  *Measured:* the corpus has 13 errors fewer and none more. *If decided
  otherwise:* the constant.
- **P191. A strict comparison of an ordinary value typed `unknown` with
  `undefined` or `null` narrows it, and a data position is left as it is.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *Decision:*
  `assume_value` of `src/narrow.rs` gives the value that type in the true
  branch. *Tests:* `tests/round9_gaps.rs`. *If decided otherwise:*
  `assume_value`.
- **P192. A type predicate narrows a value to the asserted type where the
  asserted type is assignable to a member of the value's type and no member is
  assignable to it.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner
  ruling. *The case:* a `Record<string, unknown>` narrows to the record type the
  predicate names, which `readSharedSpaceCatalog` needs once its storage type
  has no `any`. *Decision:* `assume_call` of `src/narrow.rs`. *Tests:*
  `tests/round9_gaps.rs`. *If decided otherwise:* `assume_call`.
- **P193. The left operand of `&&` and of `||` gives the result the part of its
  type that decides.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner
  ruling. *Decision:* the left operand of `&&` gives the result the part of its
  type that can be falsy, and the left operand of `||` the part that can be
  truthy (`deciding_part` of `src/infer.rs`); a literal position of a tuple has
  that element's type. Both were false refusals. *If decided otherwise:*
  `deciding_part`.
- **P194. A primitive of the data model is a leaf of the executor's values,
  compared by the text of the JSON codec, and a `bigint` by its digits.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It closes a
  finding of soundness in part. *The case:* a `FabricEpochNsec` copied by
  `structuredClone` became the plain record `{}`, and its text as JSON is `{}`
  whatever it holds, so every two times were equal and a place of the result
  kept the time of another message. *Decision:* `stored` of `exec/executor.ts`
  keeps such a value, `copyOfData` of `exec/store.ts` copies arrays and plain
  records alone, the walks of the store do not enter it, `canonical` gives it
  the text of the JSON codec of fabric values, and the adapter writes it to the
  storage as it is. *What it leaves:* 40 places of the executor that form a text
  with `JSON.stringify` were not read (question 472). *Tests:*
  `exec/test/window.test.ts`. *If decided otherwise:* `canonical`.
- **P195. The instance takes built-ins from the harness under names it does not
  have, and never in place of one it has.** The coordinator's decision of
  2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It is a stand-in of a measurement. *The
  case:* the copies of FabriChat and Home import 25 names of `commonfabric` that
  the executor lacks. *Decision:* the option `builtins` of the instance, which
  `CompiledPieceOptions` passes on. The harness hands the runtime's own for the
  pure ones and constants, for one fixed user who owns every space, for those
  that read the acting principal, the owner a label attests, or the access list
  of a space. *If decided otherwise:* each as an observation with a class of its
  own, read through the adapter (question 460).
- **P196. The harness of FabriChat runs with the write policies, the added
  integrity and the write authorizations removed from the schemas.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It is a stand-in
  of a measurement. *The case:* with the schemas as the crate emits them, no
  send of the room commits and Home's first commit is refused, for three
  refusals of the preparation. *Decision:* `compare/fabrichat/scale.ts` gives
  the schemas without the three members unless `SCALE_POLICIES` is `keep`. *What
  it costs:* the preparation of the compiled arm checks no policy, so its
  figures are a lower bound. *If decided otherwise:* the three questions 455 to
  457 answered, and the harness run with `keep`.
- **P197. The corpus run on the runner path answers a `wish` from a table.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It is a stand-in
  of a measurement. *Decision:* `compare/runner-corpus.ts` answers a `wish` from
  the seeded home of `compare/wish-home.ts` through the option `wishes`, and
  leaves a module out for a `wish` only under `--resume` and `--serving`.
  *Measured:* 28 of the 40 modules that were left out start. *If decided
  otherwise:* the runtime's own `wish` on the runner path.
- **P200. A place of the result that holds an array of the same length with
  another value at every position is written once, at the path of the array.**
  The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. It stands
  beside P83. *The case:* the window of the newest 100 messages of a room was
  written member by member, 100 writes and 100 records, twice, for each send.
  *Decision:* `differsThroughout` in `Instance.#place`; the record given is that
  of the output at the path of the array. *Measured:* a send at 100 messages
  takes 265 ms where it took 620. *Tests:* `exec/test/window.test.ts`. *If
  decided otherwise:* `differsThroughout` (question 464).
- **P210. The serving loop of `listenCompiledServingMemoryServer` reads the
  space of its runtimes from the store where the caller's policy leaves
  `storeReadThrough` unset.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no
  owner ruling. *The case:* every test and measurement of milestone 6 ran its
  serving runtimes reading over a session, which is not what a toolshed runs,
  and an edit of a title followed the board for it. *Decision:* the helper sets
  `storeReadThrough: true` unless the caller's policy says otherwise, as the
  bootstrap of a toolshed does. *Tests:* `compiled-serving.test.ts`, the case
  that counts the reads from the store. *If decided otherwise:* the policy in
  `serving-memory-server.deno.ts` (questions 452 and 469).
- **P410. A memo entry that read a write that did not reach storage is marked
  and compared with what is stored.** The coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23;
  it is no owner ruling. *The case:* with 0 stored at `x` and an output `y` that
  is twice `x`, a handler stages 1 at `x`, reads `y` through a handle, which
  evaluates `y` to 2 inside the event's transaction
  (`scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §5.3), and throws. An entry of `y` that
  stays current and unstored has 2 stored by the next demand, beside a stored
  `x` of 0. The same holds for a cone instance evaluated before the body
  of a later event of the batch, or in the derivation transaction behind it,
  against a write of an event that the wave's commit requeues or withdraws.
  *Decision:* a write is discarded when it did not reach storage and no memo
  entry holds it as unstored: a write of a handler body whose transaction did
  not commit, whether it was rejected, aborted, withdrawn or requeued, and a
  side-write whose entry is dropped. The scheduler matches the address of a
  discarded write again, with what is stored, which marks the entries evaluated
  after the write; a marked entry is compared with what is stored when it is
  next needed, and is evaluated again where a read differs. One rule covers a
  body that throws, a refused transaction and a conflict. A derived write that
  the memo holds as unstored is not discarded, and P10 keeps its rule for the
  own side-writes of a cone instance that failed at the bound
  (`scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §1.5, I3, §3.5, §5.5, §10.4 and its question
  62; `execution-and-storage.md` §3.3; `plan-and-label-templates.md` §5.4).
  *Alternative:* drop every entry evaluated in a transaction that did not
  commit, and every entry of a later transaction of the batch that read one of
  its writes; it evaluates again the cone instances that read no discarded
  write. *Tests:* none. Read in source and not run: the prototype's executor at
  `aabee19586` undoes the store's changes of a transaction that does not commit
  (`Instance.#abort` in `base/pattern-compiler/exec/executor.ts`, with
  `Store.undo`), each undone change marks the entries that read the position,
  and a marked entry is evaluated again where a position it read changed after
  its evaluation (`Instance.#current`). *If decided otherwise:* the items of
  §3.5 and §3.3 named above (question 510).
- **P411. `Object.fromEntries` records the enumeration of its argument and the
  value of each key, and `concat` the enumeration of an array operand.** The
  coordinator's decision of 2026-11-23; it is no owner ruling. *The case:*
  with no observation for `Object.fromEntries(e)`,
  `(pairs) => Object.keys(Object.fromEntries(pairs)).length` has an empty
  footprint: the body is handed an argument without `pairs`, and its result is
  wrong (`footprint-analysis.md` §9.2; the label covers what the body is
  given). The length of `v.concat(w)` depends on `w` in the same way.
  *Decision:* in §3.4 there, the rule the
  document applies to `new Map(v)`: `enumeration` at a projection `e` and
  `value` at `e/*/0`, and `value` at a key that is a projection where the body
  built the pairs; `concat` records `enumeration` at an operand that is a
  projection of array type. *Alternative:* a record whose key set is tracked,
  with the observation made by the later `Object.keys`; the abstract domain has
  no such value. *Tests:* none. The crate at `aabee19586` records nothing for
  `Object.fromEntries` (`footprint.rs`, the arm `("Object", "fromEntries")`),
  and records the enumeration of an array operand of `concat`. *If decided
  otherwise:* the two rows and the paragraph below the table of objects
  (question 511).

**The scope of the storage decisions** (the coordinator's recommendation to
the owner, 2026-11-18; not an owner ruling). Read in source after round 5:
today's storage receives a patch from the writer and stores it, and sends
the whole document to every subscriber. The costs that P20 and P25 to P28
address, what a subscriber receives for one small change of a long list,
merging pushes into an array stored in chunks, and finding the chunk of a
key, are properties of the storage layer and hold for today's runtime as
much as for the compiled language. Chunked storage of long arrays is
therefore a requirement on the storage layer, decided there: a sync that
carries a patch to a subscriber that holds the prior version, and storage
that maintains the chunk layout so that the four mergeable operations keep
merging. This design keeps of it what it needs: the split points, P22 (a
cone holds a reference to a collection it places), and the bound that the
change of one row writes and delivers an amount that does not depend on the
length. P20 and P25 to P28 stay recorded as the shape the design expects
of storage.

## Open, and needing the owner

Each entry names where the question is stated in full and the assumption the
documents make until it is answered. "ES", "SS", and "FA" are
`execution-and-storage.md`, `scheduler-and-serving-loop.md`, and
`footprint-analysis.md`; a question number is an entry of that document's
open-questions section, and the other numbers are findings of the cross-read
record.

**Label rules.** Each changes what Contextual Flow Control decides, so the
answer goes to the specification with the document.

7. **The integrity of a closure's factory value** (record, section 2).
   *Assumed, and written into the specification:* it takes no integrity
   from its captures.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

10. **A value passed on unchanged is a reference** (FA question 2).
    *Assumed:* yes, as today, which makes "the stored value is a link to
    the original" a rule of the language. The values of the prototype's
    corpus run need the rule. What a write stores where the reference
    leads into what the write replaces is question 84 of ES.
11. **A label-only change** (SS question 8). *Assumed:* a demanded kept
    output is instantiated again without running value code.

**Transactions, identity, and spaces.**

15. **Commits across spaces** (SS question 6). *Assumed:* one ordered,
    non-atomic sequence: the creation of a space an `inSpace` request
    creates, the allocation record, access changes, the batches in other
    spaces, then home. The ruling has the allocation recorded before the
    step in the other space; the creation of the space comes first here
    because a record committed before it could name a space that never
    exists (ES §5.6, SS §9.4).
16. **Demand across spaces** (SS question 5). *Assumed:* a serving
    runtime's session on another space counts as demand there.
17. **`inSpace` on a statically resolved callee in the reactive tier**
    (A9). Settled with the ruling on `asInstance()`: a call through
    `inSpace` is an instance of its own, with its own argument and
    result documents, and is not compiled into the surrounding
    instance ([Decided](#decided)). The entry keeps its number.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

21. **Event order per space** (SS question 10). *Assumed:* the proposal of
    Scheduler v2 §7.5.

**Clients.**

23. **A predicted refusal** (SS question 7). *Assumed:* no speculative
    result, a mark on the control, and the event is still sent.

**Migration.**

25. **Settled effect results** (ES question 2). *Assumed:* copied forward,
    so that a migrated instance does not request again.
26. **Retired documents and refused sources** (ES questions 3 and 4).
    *Assumed:* deletion after thirty days without a read, and a space
    that holds an instance whose source the compiler refuses is not
    switched.
27. **State inside a compiled-in sub-pattern** (ES §5.7, §9.3). Matching it
    to a call site needs the builder form, so an instance of a space
    switched after stage 6 loses that state.

**The language.**

28. **When the identity-alias typings are published** (A14). Until they
    are, an accepted program can show an editor error, against rule 2 of
    the language subset.
29. **Two senses of "cause"** (A17): what a transaction is opened for, and
    the seed of an identifier, as in `.for(cause)`.
30. **`inspectConfLabel` on an interim value** (K3). The plan document
    instantiates the value's template when asked; the inventory answers
    `notAvailable`. The ruling says an interim value is not labeled.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

32. **Context reads in the pattern body** (`builtin-inventory.md`, open
    question 10). The language subset refuses `eventKey` and
    `currentPrincipal` there and no document decides the others. Today
    every one but `equals` and `getPatternEnvironment` throws in a pattern
    body. *Assumed:* the others are legal there, as in a `lift`.
33. **"Evaluate the same gates"** (K18). The ruling has clients evaluate
    the same gates as the server. One gate cannot be evaluated on a
    client: the egress ceiling of an effect a handler requests depends on
    sink ceilings that are server configuration. The overview now says a
    client evaluates the gates it can from the plan and the data it holds.
34. **The label metadata of a label that depends on a value**
    (`plan-and-label-templates.md`, open question 16). The stored label of
    a conditional, a chosen child, or a prefix fold differs with the
    condition's value, so a reader of the label in another instance learns
    something about the condition.
35. **What `resultOwnerOf` returns** (`plan-and-label-templates.md`, open
    question 17). It returns the result of a verifier read, which
    contributes no label today. The specification calls an exposed
    verification result a labeled observation.
36. **An effect request that holds a reference** (F1). *Written into
    `plan-and-label-templates.md` §3.14 and the specification:* the
    transaction that checks the egress ceiling follows the references the
    request holds as far as the built-in serializes, and checks the ceiling
    on the join. The other correction, a request that reads the content of
    its members, would put that content's label on every other write of
    the handler.
37. **Side-writes of a failed cone.** *Written into
    `plan-and-label-templates.md` §5.2:* a failed cone's writes to a state
    cell, a cell through a handle, a created cell, or an anchors document
    are withdrawn, which leaves it visible that the write did not happen,
    as it is today; a child's argument and an effect's request take the
    error state.
**From the second round of passes.** "PL" is
`plan-and-label-templates.md`, "LS" is `language-subset.md`, and "BI" is
`builtin-inventory.md`. Each is written into the documents as an
assumption.

39. **What a withdrawn write takes with it** (PL §4.5, §4.6, question
    28). The ruling withdraws a derived write alone on a conflict. Other
    writes of the transaction can have been computed from a value or a
    label it staged. *Assumed:* those are withdrawn with it and the rest
    commits. The alternative evaluates and checks them again at the
    commit.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

41. **Where a result is split** (ES §4.10, question 32). *Assumed:* the
    split points are the root of a kept output, a row of a kept
    collection, and a node of the rendered tree at any depth; a part is
    split off at 1,024 bytes and merged back under half of that, and a
    document holds at most 65,536; the properties of a rendered node stay
    with the node. Provisional (P20): the first number is the constant
    `PART_MIN_BYTES`, no split point becomes a part for the size of the
    document that holds it, and an array over the second number is stored
    in chunks. The numbers are placeholders for stage 4 to measure.
42. **An instance made again under the identity of one torn down** (ES
    §2.8, question 33). By ruling the removal of an element deletes
    nothing stored under its key, and an element that returns under the
    same key reads what its state cells held ([Decided](#decided)). The
    ruling is on the state cells and the operation state that an
    element body declares, over an array of references, an array of
    plain values in place, and the result of another per-element
    construct alike. It does not speak of an instance. *Assumed:* an
    instance made again under the identity of one torn down finds the
    stored state where that is not yet deleted, and the documents of a
    torn-down instance are deleted after the retention period of ES
    §9.6. A link to a torn-down instance held elsewhere reads the last
    stored values. That covers an instance that a `lift` or a
    `computed` makes, which is not about a per-element construct, and a
    child of an element body, in each of the three cases: the key
    returns when the same resolved address, the same value, or the same
    upstream key stands in the collection again. The alternative for
    the child of an element body keeps its documents as the state cells
    of the body are kept, so that a child made again always finds its
    state. By ruling a child of an element body that is called through
    `asInstance()` is not torn down when its key leaves, in each of the
    three cases, so the assumption covers a child without the modifier.
43. **A failed evaluation of a computation that makes instances** (PL
    §3.14). *Assumed:* the instances of the last evaluation stay, and
    their arguments take the error state.
44. **A cone that failed on a time or memory budget** (ES question 34).
    *Assumed:* as at the bound, it is not evaluated again until an input
    changes.
45. **The acting principal of a space-scoped evaluation** (SS §9.3,
    question 34). *Assumed:* none, as today. So a change of demand runs
    as the demanding principal only for that principal's own scope, and
    an `inSpace` instantiation by a space-scoped computation is refused.
46. **A kept output computed before a handler body** (ES §1.6). *Written
    in:* the event's transaction stores it; where the body read it by
    address it is instantiated and checked before the read, commits under
    that label, and its cone is evaluated again behind the batch.
47. **A container captured by an inline handler that reads only scalars
    below it** (`footprint-analysis.md` §8.5). Under the binding ruling
    the container is one link, where today the scalars are copied when
    the binding is made. The stream then stays the same when such a
    scalar changes. *Assumed:* the link.
48. **Captures of an inline pattern** (PL §3.15, questions 23 and 24).
    *Assumed:* an inline pattern instantiated in a function body binds
    its captures by the rule for a handler binding, and a pattern closure
    of the reactive tier keeps the closure rule, which copies.
49. **A `computed` that instantiates a pattern is not promoted** (LS
    §6.1), because promotion would compile the call into the surrounding
    instance and change which documents exist.
50. **`inSpace` and `asScope` on an instantiation in a computation** (PL
    §3.14; BI question 11). *Assumed:* legal, as in a handler.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

52. **Trigger reads lost at a restart** (PL §3.10, question 29). A body
    with a sampled read can be evaluated because of a change at an
    address it does not read again, and after a restart that address's
    label is not joined. *Assumed:* accepted, equal to today. The
    alternative stores those reads with the basis rows.
53. **An explicit cause is not salted** (PL §1.3, question 30), so an
    observer who can list documents can test a guess of a low-entropy
    cause. *Assumed:* as today.
54. **Logs** (the overview). Whether a body can pass labeled data to
    `console`. Nothing is assumed; the footprint counts the arguments as
    read.
55. **A cone that reads a stale stored value of an instance that is not
    loaded** (ES §2.4, SS §4.4). *Assumed:* the read does not wait. It
    returns what is stored, the instance is loaded and the writer
    evaluated, and the reading cone is evaluated again. An output
    computed from the stale value can be stored in between. The
    alternative withdraws the derivation.
56. **Standing demand still loads an instance** (SS §4.4). The ruling on
    reading a current stored value is applied to an event's reads and to
    a one-shot pull. *Assumed:* a session, a render sink, an effect, or a
    materializer that depends on the instance loads it, because the
    scheduler learns of later input changes only through a loaded
    instance's entries.
57. **A write through a handle by an instance that is not loaded** (SS
    §4.4, §5.3). Nothing stored names the writer, so the check cannot
    tell that the value is stale. *Assumed:* the read returns what is
    stored.
58. **Stream index rows across a source update** (SS §5.1). *Assumed:*
    a row is kept, and an event for a binding the new plan lacks cannot
    be run.

**From the corrections after the second cross-read.**

59. **An explicit cause in the reactive tier** (LS §4.7, question 17; PL
    §1.3, question 31). *Assumed:* `.for(cause)` there takes a string
    literal, which takes the place of the declaration's name. A cause
    that is data is legal only in a function body.
60. **A `computed` that binds a handler is not promoted** (LS §6.1),
    because promotion would turn a binding made in a function body into
    one of the reactive tier. Ten `computed` calls of the corpus fail on
    this alone. It widens question 49.
61. **A built-in that needs a requester, where no principal demands it**
    (BI "The requester of a request"; SS §6.2, question 36). *Assumed:*
    `agent`, a cross-space or clearance-reading `sqliteQuery`, and
    `navigateTo` have user or session scope whatever computes their
    request, and are not requested without a demanding principal, as
    today. The principal of a completion's transaction and of a
    materializer's run is not decided. It extends question 45.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

63. **The allocation record of a created space stays when the unit that
    asked for it does not commit** (PL §4.6, question 32). *Assumed:*
    accepted, as the one exception to "no write commits that used a write
    that does not".
64. **Tearing down an instance in another space** (SS §9.3, question 40;
    ES §2.8). *Assumed:* the home transaction writes the mark of the
    instance it made, and the other space's loop marks the instances that
    belong to it there.
65. **`asScope` on a child** (ES §4.6, question 52). *Assumed:* the scope
    changes only the child's state cell documents. A kept output of the
    child that reads no such cell is stored once for the space, where
    today the whole result cell is per user or session.
66. **Spaces created without a name by the current runtime** are not
    found by a compiled instance, because the allocation record is named
    by the request's own identifier (ES §5.6).
67. **A handle below the cut of a recursive type** (FA §2.2, request 22).
    *Assumed:* the body is handed handles down to the cut and finds
    nothing below it, the one exception to "narrowing the argument does
    not change what the body does".
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

69. **`sqliteDatabase`** (BI, LS §4.7). *Assumed:* legal in the reactive
    tier only, with table declarations that are static; a database first
    written with no acting principal has no owner, so a rule that names
    the owner admits nobody.
70. **A handler that reads a materializer that cannot run ahead of it**
    (SS §7.2). *Written in:* the event holds its place until the
    materializer has run. A materializer that stays invalid keeps the
    event waiting.

**From the rulings of 2026-11-13.** Each is written into the documents
as an assumption.

76. **The state of an occurrence among equal elements** (PL question
    36). Which state an occurrence has depends on the equal elements
    before it in the collection, which the label of its own position
    does not hold. *Assumed:* accepted as a residual. It is the same
    over an array of references, where equal elements are links that
    resolve to one address, and over an array of plain values in place,
    where they are equal values. An element of the result of another
    per-element construct has its upstream key, so its state depends on
    the equal elements of the first source of the chain and not on
    equal values in the result.
77. **The argument of a `.for(tag)` instance on a later event** (PL
    question 39). *Assumed:* not written again. The alternative writes it
    on every event, as a computation does.
78. **Which bodies the warning for an instantiation without a cause
    covers** (LS question 26). *Assumed:* a `lift`, a `computed`, an
    `assert`, and an authored function one of them or the reactive tier
    calls; not a `handler`, an `action`, or an inline event handler.
79. **The label of the error state after a refused send** (PL question
    38). *Assumed:* the join of the request's label, what was sent and
    received before, and the label the refused check was evaluated on.
80. **The instance of a tool call** (BI question 6). *Assumed:*
    identified by the built-in's operation, the request or turn, the
    ordinal of the model call, and the position of the tool call, not by
    the identifier the model supplies; made in the operation's space at
    the result's scope; torn down when the request or turn settles.
81. **The label of a database declaration's state document** (PL
    question 40). *Assumed:* empty.
82. **Which initializers are static for a default** (LS question 25).
    *Assumed:* a literal, an array or object literal of static
    initializers, and a reference to a constant with one.
83. **When a space is switched** (ES question 69). *Assumed:* the
    deployment names the spaces, the switch runs at an activation before
    the first cycle and evaluates nothing, and each instance has its
    first compiled evaluation at its first load.
84. **A space with an instance whose source the compiler refuses** (ES
    questions 4 and 70). *Assumed:* it is not switched; when the builder
    path is retired it is switched without that instance, which stops
    running until its source is updated. It extends question 26.
85. **Reversing a switch** (ES question 71). *Assumed:* not reversed.
86. **A link between a switched space and one that is not** (ES question
    72; SS question 41). *Assumed:* the reader reads the value and label
    as the other path stored them, so the tighter labels hold only along
    switched spaces.
87. **Events across the switch** (ES question 73). *Assumed:* the switch
    starts once the builder path has handled the queued events; a later
    event on a stream whose identifier is not kept is deferred and then
    dropped.
88. **How a validation run compares the two paths** (ES question 74).
    *Assumed:* between two spaces, one on each path. Nothing is designed.
89. **A client that holds spaces of both kinds** (SS question 42).
    *Assumed:* one runtime runs, per space, the path the space's mark
    names.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

93. **Whether a write through a handle of `unknown` is refused,** on the
    ground that a write needs a specific type, with `Cell<T>` then
    assignable to `ReadonlyCell<unknown>`. Raised by the owner, not
    ruled. The prototype is counting the corpus sites that write through
    such a handle.
<!-- The list restarts so that the numbers below stay as cited. -->

97. **A default on a type that names `undefined`** (LS question 34).
    *Assumed:* the type keeps the named `undefined`.
98. **A truthiness test on a value of type `unknown`.** *Assumed:*
    accepted, as a test of presence. The ruling names the test against
    `undefined` alone, so it can be read as refusing this.
99. **The declared type of a bound path whose prefix a condition
    narrows** (LS question 35). *Assumed:* the declared type is taken at
    the last step, and the prefix keeps its narrowing so that the
    property is found. The alternative refuses a path below a narrowed
    prefix.
100. **Which read and append the read-then-push warning reports** (LS
    question 36). *Assumed:* any read of the list in a body that calls
    `push` or `pushAll` on it, and not `addUnique`. This reports more
    sites than today's classifier.
101. **How the cones of a plan are partitioned** (PL question 44).
    *Assumed:* the partition the prototype chose.
102. **A statically resolved pattern on a cycle of calls** (PL question
    45; LS question 37). *Assumed:* refused. What the builder does today
    is not verified.
103. **How value code reads the child a dynamic key chose** (PL question
    46). *Assumed:* it is handed every child. `execution-and-storage.md`
    §2.2 gives `ConeHost.slot` no key, which disagrees with PL §3.18.
    The assumption was enough for the three corpus modules with such a
    read that the prototype's executor ran.
104. **The plan record of `wish`** (PL questions 47 and 48). *Assumed:*
    one operation of kind `wish`, whose result is read through slots
    rooted at the operation and labeled with the request joined with
    one dynamic entry for the search, with no integrity. A query that
    is not a constant is assumed to take the widest part. `wish` in a
    function body is assumed refused, and `language-subset.md` does not
    yet say so.
105. **The plan record of `reduce` in the reactive tier** (PL question
    49). *Assumed:* an operation of kind `reduce` over a step cone and a
    collection of its own, with the label a `fold` joined with the
    initial value.
106. **Three smaller records** (PL questions 50 to 52): the source of a
    scan, the positions after an array spread, and a write through a
    link that an instantiation or an effect returned. Each is assumed
    as PL states it.
107. **The template entries of a constructed value** (PL question 53):
    a rendered tree under `$UI`, or a record used as one value.
    *Assumed:* an entry per path, with view-node paths `props/<name>`
    and `children/<n>`, and a join where the value is observed whole.
    `execution-and-storage.md` has to agree on the view-node paths.
108. **What the hash of a body's code covers, and which slots carry a
    declared label** (PL questions 54 and 55). *Assumed:* the module
    and the binding; and no declared label on an `identity` slot or an
    in-place `shape` slot.
109. **What the compiler reports about label flow** (PL questions 56
    and 57). *Assumed:* it reports a confidentiality clause that no
    ceiling clause subsumes, unless a `Policy` atom is involved, though
    an exchange rule could make the clause fit at run time; and it
    takes a declared integrity as complete for a failure, though the
    runtime joins label components on both axes, so that a declaration
    is a lower bound.
110. **A JSX tag that names a factory value the instance computed** (PL
    question 58). *Assumed:* refused. `language-subset.md` names no
    diagnostic for it.
111. **Two refusals that look intended** in the corpus. A handle from
    `key` on an optional property, of type `Cell<T | undefined>`, given
    where a handler declares an optional `Writable<T>` (FabriChat's
    `room.tsx`); and an array of pattern results given where a cell of
    an array of that pattern's result type is declared
    (`quick-capture.tsx`). *Assumed:* both refused, as
    `language-subset.md` §7.5 reads.
112. **An input constraint on what expression code reads** (PL
    question 59). *Assumed:* constrained as a body is.
113. **Whether the compiler should decide write-floor and writer-fit
    for a write through a handle.** With no declared label on an
    `identity` slot (question 108), every such template has a term the
    compiler cannot evaluate, so it decides these two for expression
    code and for bodies that read values alone. *Assumed:* that stands,
    and the runtime check covers the rest.
114. **A UI contract whose surface is in the embedding pattern** (PL
    question 61). The chain of enclosing elements continues through a
    pattern written as a tag below the surface, and ends where a
    pattern is called and its tree is placed through a computed value.
    The second case occurs once, in FabriChat's thread composer.
    *Assumed:* it is reported, as a warning. The alternative suppresses
    the report for a pattern that is compiled into another.
115. **What is hashed** (PL questions 62 and 63). *Assumed:* every hash
    is the tagged value hash the runtime uses, with no tag for the kind
    of record; only a recursive type gets a `$defs` entry, named by its
    declared name; code is hashed as its source for a cone and as the
    module and binding for a body.

116. **What identifies the pattern in its `TransformedBy`, and which
    pattern it is for code compiled into another** (PL question 64).
    Settled for which pattern by the ruling of 2026-11-19 ([Decided](#decided)):
    code of a pattern B compiled into a pattern A mints B's atom, the
    pattern in whose source the expression is written. *Assumed* for the
    identity: the pattern's module and binding.
117. **What the corpus comparison compares.** The runtime copies values
    where the plan passes references. *Assumed:* the comparison is made
    on dereferenced labels. The static part the runtime joins from a
    module's argument schema is separated by its origin and expected
    as a difference, by ruling.

119. **The runtime does not label an `ifElse` result with its
    condition** (PL question 69). Where the chosen branch is a
    reference, `forwardReference` writes the reference and a link to it
    with two raw writes that are not recorded as link writes, and no
    stored entry holds the condition's label. It reaches a reader only
    through the static entry joined from the argument schema, and only
    where the condition's input schema declares it. Where the branch is
    a literal, the stored value gets the join. This is confirmed by a
    test over three cases, not committed. It is a finding against the
    runtime, and by the owner's decision it is not filed, because the
    builder path is retired; what matters is that a conditional in
    pattern code has the right label in the compiled path. *Assumed:*
    the template, which joins the condition and the
    chosen branch, stands, and the comparison is made with the
    runtime's static part included for a conditional.

120. **Where the pattern's `TransformedBy` is added** (PL questions 71
    and 72). The owner confirmed on 2026-11-19 that every kept output
    carries it; the rest is open, and question 302 is the owner's design
    for a value passed on from an argument. *Assumed:* at kept outputs
    only, with no condition, as one
    entry at the root of the result document. A promoted `computed`
    that passes a value unchanged to a child argument, a write target,
    or an effect request then has fewer atoms than today. What a reader
    that dereferences a link gets of the link's atom is not stated.
121. **Two labels the comparison found the documents wrong or silent
    about** (PL questions 73 and 74). *Assumed:* the label of an event
    slot is what the event arrived with, and a declared label is not a
    lower bound there; and no `TransformedBy` is minted beside a label
    that only a declaration gives.
122. **An output of a computation that threw, in the comparison** (PL
    question 76). The runtime stores no label there; the compiled path
    stores an error state under the output's template. *Assumed:* such
    an output is not a row of the comparison and is no further
    exception to "equal or tighter". The alternative counts it as an
    exception by ruling. The comparison met seven such outputs.
123. **A record for a reference that a site of a body made** (PL
    question 77). *Assumed:* a path that holds a handle a `createCell`
    site returned takes the body's `derive` template, and the plan has
    no member that names the site. The alternative adds such a member,
    which gives a constant template where the cell is a state cell.
124. **How much of a handler's template is on a link it writes** (PL
    question 79). By ruling the link carries at least the label of the
    event. *Assumed:* the handler's whole template joined with the
    label of the reference, which equals what the runtime stores
    today. The alternative joins the event and the reference alone.
    For a `lift` or a `computed` that passes a handle on at a result
    path the link keeps the label of the reference alone.
125. **Where the stream of a binding of an element body is stored** (PL
    question 78). Not applicable as a question about the plan, by the
    ruling that value code places a stream and that no record names
    where it is stored ([Decided](#decided)): each element of the
    assembled collection holds the link that the cone instance of its
    key placed, and a reader of the plan alone cannot say where a
    stream is. Settled by ruling as well: a collection among the
    children of a view node is one nested child, with its elements at
    `children/<n>/*`, so two collections among the children of one node
    are two child positions, and a child written after a collection has
    a static position. The prototype's plans hold a list of result
    paths with a kind for each `*` (prototype note 372), which the
    design does not have. The same over an array of references, an
    array of plain values in place, and the result of another
    per-element construct. The entry keeps its number.
126. **A schema of the plan and the schema the runtime stores an input
    under** (PL question 80). *Assumed:* the comparison stores inputs
    under the runtime's schema. The documents do not say how a schema
    of the plan names a policy.
127. **The `link` entry at the position of a handle that is only
    passed on** (PL question 81). The runtime stores there what the
    reference declares, which repeats the label of the cell's type.
    *Assumed:* it is not part of the handle's label, and the stamp of
    the run that wrote the link is. The runtime reads nothing at such
    a position, so the template can be looser than today by that
    stamp; the comparison met no such row.
128. **The event type of an inline handler that declares none** (PL
    question 82). An `on*` attribute of a host element expects no
    type. *Assumed:* `unknown`, so the handler reads nothing of its
    event. The alternatives refuse a parameter without an annotation
    there, or declare the event type of each attribute of each host
    element.
129. **The existence label of a path that a write removed** (PL
    question 83). The runtime leaves it in place, so a read of a list
    a handler emptied carries the clauses its former elements were
    created under. *Assumed:* the compiled path keeps it, equal to
    today. The alternative removes it with the path.
130. **A stream that the elements of a collection hold inside a value**
    (PL question 84). Not applicable, by the ruling that value code
    places a stream and that no record names where it is stored
    ([Decided](#decided)). A stream inside a value that one element
    holds, as `example[UI]` over an array of the results of patterns in
    `patterns/examples/cfc-trusted-component-examples/` (208 bindings),
    is stored where the element cone passes the member on with the
    marker in it. A further 5 bindings of the corpus have a stream that
    is read through a member of the element by name, as `entry.node`.
    The source is an array of plain values in place, an array written
    in place in the pattern body whose members the instance computes,
    or the result of another per-element construct whose elements hold
    the stream of a binding of that construct's body. Over an array of
    references the case does not arise, because a stream behind a
    reference is no binding's marker. The entry keeps its number.
131. **The declared label of an element's handle in the compiled
    path** (PL question 85). Settled by ruling: the handle of an
    element is read at the element's position in the source
    collection, and nothing of the `map` coordinator's join is in its
    label. Settled by PL's own rule: an entry of origin `link` at that
    position is in the label of a handle the body resolves or reads or
    writes through. Open: whether such a handle, where it is resolved
    and not read through, also carries the label that the declaration
    of the source collection gives the element. A clause a list
    declares for itself is stored at the root of the list's document
    and is consumed by a read of content, not by a read of which
    reference a position holds. In the runs observed the argument
    document of the element's instance has no `link` entry at
    `element`, and the handler has the list's clause from the
    coordinator's join alone, so the two descriptions the question
    gave of one label are two labels. *Assumed:* the handle carries
    the declared label, which is equal to today for `askToRetire` of
    `patterns/system/profile-picker/profile-picker.tsx`. Without it
    that write is tighter in confidentiality and has no atom
    (question 138). No record of the plan holds the declared label.
    Not determined by a run: whether a list that declares a clause
    for its items alone gives the link at `element` a `link` entry.
    The open part is about an array of references, which the observed
    runs are over. Over an array of plain values in place no link
    stands below the position, and the assumption gives the handle the
    same declared label of the list. Over the result of another
    per-element construct the element's label is what the template of
    the upstream output gives the position, and nothing is open.
133. **A written path that holds a link, for a write edge with no
    reference** (PL question 87). *Assumed:* the row is not compared
    where the run stored a link at the written path, and is counted
    apart. Not stated: whether one write can have an edge with a
    reference and an edge without, as the prototype emits.
134. **A label the runtime fails to read, and a slot whose path
    crosses a cycle of links** (PL question 88). *Assumed:* the row
    is not compared, and in the compiled path the evaluation that
    reads the slot fails as a body that throws does.

136. **A binding that a computation in an element body makes** (PL
    question 90). A binding made in a function body is named by what
    it holds and by no place, and everything an element body holds is
    per element key. *Assumed:* the first governs, so two occurrences
    that bind equal state from a `computed` or a `lift` have one
    stream. That is the same over an array of references (two links
    that resolve to one address, passed on), an array of plain values
    in place (equal copied values), and the result of another
    per-element construct (two elements with different keys that copy
    or pass on equal state).
138. **A write row whose template is empty beside the coordinator's
    join** (PL question 96). Where every clause a run stores for a
    handler's write is of the `map` coordinator's join, the template
    has no clause and mints no atom, and the run mints one. The row is
    tighter in confidentiality and looser in integrity by that atom.
    *Assumed:* it is counted apart as looser in integrity and is not
    among the deliberate exceptions. The alternatives count it as an
    exception by ruling, or mint on every `derive` of a write edge.
    One fixture has such a row and the corpus has none. The row arises
    in all three cases. What the coordinator's join holds today
    differs: the clauses of the list's own document over an array of
    references, those of the other elements as well over an array of
    plain values in place, and, over the result of another per-element
    construct, which today is an array of links to the upstream
    elements' result cells, what it holds for an array of references.
140. **The transaction that creates an instance outside a handler**
    (ES question 77). *Assumed:* one transaction that writes the
    argument and evaluates nothing, so that a new instance settles in
    two transactions. The alternative evaluates in the creating
    transaction. The derived count of two transactions to settle
    rests on the assumption.

**From the prototype's executor.** Each is written into the documents
